spec: Set MATRIX_LR = 0.03 for Muon, to bracket the optimum from below.

title: Lower total batch to 2**17
spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 (or reduce device batch if the grad-accum divisibility assert fails). Test whether many more small steps beat larger batches in 300 s.

title: Embedding LR 0.9
spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR = 0.9 (Adam on token embeddings). Short runs often benefit from faster embedding learning.

title: Muon beta 0.97 final
spec: Raise the final Muon momentum from 0.95 to 0.97 for the warmdown stage. Leave the ramp unchanged.

title: Disable torch.compile dynamic overhead / use max-autotune
spec: Compile the model with mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs" if the code uses plain torch.compile. Compile time is not counted, so only throughput matters. Keep the compile and startup time under the 450 s limit.

title: Weight decay 0.3 with decay on schedule
spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.3. If the code already scales weight decay with the LR multiplier, leave that as it is.

title: Short warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to avoid early instability at the high Adam LRs and Muon LR.

title: Cosine-shaped warmdown
spec: Replace the linear warmdown in the LR multiplier function with a cosine decay. Over the warmdown portion (last 50% of progress), use mult = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1-FINAL_LR_FRAC) * 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi * t)), where t goes from 0 to 1 across the warmdown. Keep the flat phase before it. Apply to all optimizer groups, and leave the momentum schedule alone.

title: Gradient clipping 1.0
spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) just before the optimizer step. Check that it works with the grad accumulation loop.

title: Value embeddings on all layers
spec: Currently value embeddings (ResFormer style) are likely on alternating layers only. Add a value embedding to every layer, each with its own nn.Embedding(vocab, kv_dim) and a gated mix into v using the existing gate form. Put the new embedding tables in the Adam embedding group at EMBEDDING_LR. This adds parameters but little compute, and it tests whether more token-specific capacity helps in the short run.

title: Untied value embedding on every layer
spec: If value embeddings are added only on alternating layers, add them on all layers. Reuse the existing gating code and add one embedding table per layer. Check that VRAM is OK.

title: Sequence packing / shorter context 1024 to 512
spec: Halve the sequence length used for training to 512, if the sequence length is a constant imported or set in train.py and the validation call is unaffected. If it is imported from prepare.py and cannot be changed, instead set the sliding window for S layers to a quarter of the context. With shorter context, attention is cheaper, so more steps run in 300 s. Keep tokens per step equal by doubling the sequences per micro-batch, so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE becomes 128 only if memory allows. Otherwise use accumulation.

title: Depth 4 wider model
spec: Set DEPTH = 4 and ASPECT_RATIO = 96 so model_dim is 384 (3 heads of dim 128, same width as now). The shallower net is faster per step and gets more optimizer steps in 300 s. Keep everything else unchanged. Check that WINDOW_PATTERN still works with 4 layers (the last layer is forced to be long).

title: Smaller total batch size for more steps
spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64 and adjust the gradient accumulation so the micro-batch count halves. This gives twice as many optimizer updates within the 300 s budget at the cost of gradient noise.

title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon
spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations in the Muon update from 5 to 3. This makes each optimizer step cheaper, so more steps fit in the 300 s budget. Keep the quintic coefficients as they are unless the code requires a change for fewer iterations. Keep the rest of the optimizer unchanged.

title: Lower Muon weight decay
spec: Reduce WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.05 for the Muon matrix parameters. Keep the Adam groups unchanged. Lower decay lets the matrices fit the short 300 s run faster.

title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO (0.5) of the time budget. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups. Keep WARMUP_RATIO at 0.0.

title: Longer warmdown fraction
spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the last 70% of the 300 s budget. Keep the linear shape and all other hyperparameters unchanged.

title: Global gradient-norm clipping
spec: Before each optimizer step, compute the global L2 norm of all parameter gradients and rescale them so the norm is at most 1.0, using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ on the model parameters. Leave the optimizer hyperparameters unchanged. This guards against loss spikes at the high peak learning rates, which could otherwise waste steps in a short run.

title: Layer-wise learning-rate decay for Adam groups
spec: Give each transformer block's Adam-managed scalar parameters a learning rate that scales geometrically with depth, lr_l = SCALAR_LR * 0.85^(DEPTH-1-l), so the top layers learn fastest and the bottom layers slowest. Apply the same schedule multiplier as the existing warmdown. Muon groups and the embedding groups keep their current learning rates. This is a small, self-contained change to parameter group construction.

title: Shape-aware Muon learning-rate scaling
spec: Scale each matrix parameter's Muon update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so tall and wide matrices get comparable effective step sizes. Keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04 and the rest of the update unchanged. Apply the scale to the orthogonalized update before it is applied to the weight.

title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameter count
spec: Replace the two-matrix ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU block: a fused up-projection to 2 x hidden, split into gate and value halves, output = silu(gate) * value, then a down-projection. Set the hidden width to about 2/3 of the current 4 x model_dim so the parameter count is unchanged. Keep the Muon-managed matrices and the rest of the block as they are.

title: Looped middle block with shared weights
spec: Keep DEPTH layers in the forward pass but make the middle two blocks share one set of weights, so the forward pass runs block A, block B, block B again, then the remaining layers. Parameter count drops by one block while compute per step rises slightly. Per-position residual scalars stay separate for each application. This tests whether recurrent depth beats extra unique parameters under a fixed time budget.

title: U-Net style long skip connections
spec: Treat the transformer as an encoder-decoder with symmetric skips. Store the residual stream output of each of the first DEPTH/2 blocks. In the second half, before block i (counting from the middle), add the stored activation from the mirrored encoder block through a learnable per-channel scale initialized to zero. This is a residual-only addition with no new attention or MLP parameters beyond the scales. Keep the existing per-layer scalars and the lm_head path unchanged.

title: Tie input embedding and lm_head weights
spec: Share one matrix between the token embedding and the lm_head, removing the separate unembedding parameter and its Adam group. Initialize the shared weight with std about 0.02 and use EMBEDDING_LR for it, dropping UNEMBEDDING_LR from the optimizer setup. Multiply the logits by a fixed 1/sqrt(model_dim) scale if the logits are too large at init. This frees parameters and optimizer state for more layers or width at the same budget.

title: Bigram hash embedding at the input
spec: Add a second embedding table indexed by a hash of the previous token and the current token, with a few thousand buckets and model width output. Add its output to the token embedding before the first block. Initialize it to zero so the baseline is unchanged at the start of training.

title: Learnable per-layer attention temperature
spec: Give each attention layer a learnable scalar temperature s initialized to 1.0, and multiply the attention logits by s times the usual 1/sqrt(head_dim) scale before the softmax. Place s in the Adam-managed scalar group with the existing per-layer scalars so it uses SCALAR_LR and no weight decay. Keep QK normalization and sliding-window masks unchanged. This lets each layer adjust its sharpness of attention independently and adds only one parameter per layer.

title: Grouped-query attention with fewer KV heads
spec: Use grouped-query attention with the number of key/value heads set to one quarter of the query heads (minimum 1). Keep the number of query heads and head dimension unchanged. The smaller KV projections reduce parameters and memory traffic, which allows more steps in the fixed time budget.

title: QK-norm with learnable per-head gain
spec: After the query and key RMS normalization in each attention layer, multiply by a learnable per-head gain vector initialized to 1 (one per head, separate for q and k). Keep the attention scale otherwise unchanged and store the gains in the scalar parameter group.

title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon
spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3. This saves wall-clock per step inside the fixed 300 s budget, so more optimizer steps fit. Keep the same quintic coefficients and everything else unchanged.

title: Grouped-query attention with 2 KV heads
spec: Use grouped-query attention with num_kv_heads set to 2 for the key and value projections while keeping the number of query heads unchanged. Repeat the key and value heads across query groups before attention. This reduces attention parameters and memory traffic at the same model width.

title: Longer warmdown phase
spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the final 70% of the time budget, keeping WARMUP_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC unchanged. This tests whether a longer cooldown improves the final checkpoint.

title: Gradient norm clipping
spec: Add global gradient-norm clipping at 1.0 on all trainable parameters after the backward pass and before the optimizer steps. This stabilizes the high learning rates (EMBEDDING_LR 0.6, SCALAR_LR 0.5) in the early phase.

title: Shallower and wider model
spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 85 so model_dim is about 510, rounded to 512 to keep it a multiple of HEAD_DIM=128. Keep all other hyperparameters unchanged. This trades layers for faster steps within the fixed time budget.

title: Exponential moving average for final weights
spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Before the final evaluation call, copy the EMA weights into the model. Do not modify the evaluation call or the summary printing.

title: SwiGLU MLP instead of ReLU-squared
spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU MLP whose hidden width is set to about 2/3 of 4*model_dim, rounded to a multiple of 64, so the parameter count stays close to the baseline. Keep the same residual and normalization structure.

title: Parallel attention and MLP residual blocks
spec: Change each transformer block from sequential x = x + attn(norm(x)); x = x + mlp(norm(x)) to parallel form x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), sharing one pre-norm. Keep the existing per-layer residual scalars and window pattern. This removes one normalization and one serial dependency per layer, which can increase throughput within the fixed 300 s budget. Verify that the model still compiles and that the first-step loss is comparable.

title: Higher unembedding (lm_head) learning rate
spec: Raise UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008 and keep every other hyperparameter fixed. The lm_head is the only Adam-trained output projection, so this tests whether the output layer is under-trained at the current rate.

title: Adam-group learning-rate warmup
spec: Ramp the learning rates of the Adam-trained groups (embedding, lm_head, scalars) linearly from 10% to 100% over the first 200 optimizer steps, while Muon matrix learning rate follows the normal schedule from step 0. This protects the high-LR scalar and embedding groups during early training.

title: Uniform averaging of late checkpoints
spec: Starting at 70 percent of the time budget, after each optimizer step, add the current parameters into a running sum held in float32 on the GPU and count the number of additions. At the end of training, replace the model weights with the average of the saved snapshots before the harness evaluation runs. Do not modify the evaluation call itself. This replaces the EMA attempt, which was likely broken, with a simple uniform average over the warmdown phase, which is a different and safer weight-averaging scheme.

title: Tied input and output embeddings
spec: Tie the lm_head weight to the token embedding matrix and scale the logits by 1/sqrt(model_dim) to compensate. Remove the separate lm_head parameter group so UNEMBEDDING_LR is no longer used, and keep EMBEDDING_LR for the shared matrix.

title: Position-dependent loss weighting
spec: Multiply the per-token cross-entropy by a weight w(t) that ramps linearly from 0.5 at the first position of each sequence to 1.0 at the last position, then renormalize so the mean weight over the sequence is 1. Compute the weighted mean over tokens in the batch. Keep the optimizer, schedule, and evaluation unchanged. This shifts gradient emphasis toward later positions, where the model has more context and the bits-per-byte metric benefits most.

title: Alternative Newton-Schulz polynomial coefficients
spec: Keep 5 Newton-Schulz iterations (reducing the count was clearly harmful), but replace the polynomial coefficients used in the Muon orthogonalization with the more aggressive set (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) that pushes singular values toward 1 faster. Keep the normalization step and the rest of the Muon update unchanged. Only the coefficient tuple changes, so the diff is a one-line edit and the effect is isolated to how orthogonalized updates are shaped.

title: Final LR floor instead of zero
spec: Change FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1, so the learning rate decays to 10 percent of its initial value by the end of the 300-second budget instead of to zero. Keep the warmdown start and the linear shape as they are. Apply the floor to every parameter group, including Muon, Adam, and the scalar groups. Change nothing else. This tests whether a non-zero end learning rate helps a short run that stops before convergence.

title: Single warm restart in the LR schedule
spec: Replace the single linear warmdown with a two-cycle schedule over the time budget. The first cycle runs at full LR from 0 to 55% of the budget and then decays with a cosine to 0.3x the peak. At 55% of the budget the LR jumps back to 1.0x peak and decays with a cosine to 0 at the end. All learning rates (Muon and Adam groups) follow the same multiplier. Keep WARMUP_RATIO at 0 and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0. The purpose is to test whether a mid-run restart helps the model escape a sharp basin before the final anneal.

title: Output logit z-loss
spec: Add an auxiliary term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training loss, computed over the vocabulary dimension of the lm_head outputs. This keeps logit magnitudes bounded without changing the evaluation path.

title: Cosine warmdown with floor
spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to 0.1x peak over the warmdown window, keeping WARMDOWN_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC as they are. Compute the multiplier from elapsed time fraction. Apply the same multiplier to all optimizer groups.

title: Gradient clipping on global norm
spec: Add global gradient-norm clipping with max norm 1.0 applied after backward and before the optimizer step, across all parameters. Use torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ on model parameters. Leave the optimizer and schedules untouched.

title: Sequence length curriculum
spec: Train with a shorter context early: use sequence length 512 for the first 40% of the time budget and the full context length for the rest, adjusting the batch shape so the token count per step stays fixed. Keep the sliding-window pattern consistent with the reduced length. This raises early step throughput.

title: Sqrt-decay warmdown
spec: Replace the warmdown multiplier with sqrt-shaped decay: multiplier = sqrt(max(0, remaining_fraction)), where remaining_fraction goes from 1 to 0 across the warmdown window. Keep the constant-LR phase before warmdown unchanged. Apply uniformly to every param group.

title: Batch size halving
spec: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 and keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64, so gradient accumulation steps are halved accordingly. This doubles the number of optimizer steps in 300 s at the cost of noisier gradients. Keep all LRs unchanged.

title: Shallower and wider model
spec: Decrease DEPTH from 8 to 6 and increase ASPECT_RATIO so model_dim grows by roughly 1.33x, keeping HEAD_DIM dividing model_dim. Keep all other settings unchanged. This gives more steps per second in the fixed time budget with a wider model.

title: Embedding LR and beta tuning
spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.3 and set the beta1 of the embedding Adam group to 0.9 while the other Adam groups keep ADAM_BETAS. Only the embedding param group's hyperparameters change. This tests whether the very high embedding LR is overshooting early in training.

title: Tied embedding and unembedding
spec: Tie the lm_head weight to the token embedding weight so both share one parameter, and remove the separate UNEMBEDDING_LR Adam group by folding the shared parameter into the embedding group. Scale the output by 1/sqrt(model_dim) before the head projection to balance magnitudes. Keep the rest of the model identical.

title: Weight EMA for evaluation
spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999 updated after each optimizer step, and use the EMA weights for the final evaluation call. Keep the training forward pass on the live weights. Do not change the evaluation function itself, only which weights are loaded into the model before it is called.

title: Deeper and narrower model
spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10 while keeping model_dim approximately fixed by reducing ASPECT_RATIO so that depth times ASPECT_RATIO stays close to the current width, rounded so HEAD_DIM still divides model_dim. Keep all other settings unchanged. This tests depth versus throughput under a 300 s budget.

title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary head
spec: Add one extra linear head (model_dim to vocab, sharing no weights with lm_head) that predicts the token two positions ahead from the final hidden state. Its cross-entropy, computed on positions with a valid t+2 target, is added to the main next-token loss with weight 0.2. Only the next-token head is used at evaluation, so the reported metric is unchanged in definition. Initialize the extra head at zero to avoid perturbing early training. This is a bold change to the training objective that may improve the representation per optimizer step.

title: Parallel attention and MLP residual blocks
spec: Change each transformer block from the sequential form x = x + attn(norm(x)); x = x + mlp(norm(x)) to the parallel form x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), sharing one RMSNorm per block for both branches. Keep the per-layer residual scalars, QK normalization, sliding-window pattern and all learning rates unchanged. The parallel form removes one serial dependency per layer, which may allow the same quality with less wall-clock per step inside the fixed 300 s budget.

title: Z-loss regularizer
spec: Add an auxiliary loss of 1e-4 times the mean squared log-sum-exp of the logits over all positions, computed from the same logits used for cross-entropy. Add it to the training loss only, not the evaluation path. This stabilizes logit scale without changing the main objective.

title: Schedule-free AdamW for non-matrix parameters
spec: Replace the Adam optimizer used for the embedding, lm_head and scalar parameter groups with a schedule-free AdamW variant: keep a fast iterate z updated by Adam, and an averaged iterate x used for the forward pass and final evaluation, with interpolation coefficient 0.9 and no learning-rate warmdown for these groups. Keep the Muon matrix group and its existing LR schedule unchanged. This removes the need for the warmdown on the Adam groups, so the schedule tuning done so far applies only to Muon. Keep the existing learning rates as the base step sizes.

title: Per-head learnable QK-norm gain
spec: Apply RMSNorm to queries and keys inside attention (if not already present) and give each head a learnable scalar gain on q and k initialized to 1. The gains are trained with the scalar Adam group. This controls attention logit scale without a fixed temperature.

title: SwiGLU MLP
spec: Replace the squared-ReLU MLP in each block with a SwiGLU MLP: two up-projections to hidden size round(2/3 * 4 * model_dim) gated by SiLU, then a down-projection. Keep the parameter count close to the baseline by using that hidden width. Applies to all layers.

title: Batch-size ramp from 2^17 to 2^19
spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 and linearly increase the effective batch (via gradient accumulation steps) to 2**19 over the first 40% of the time budget, then hold it. Round accumulation steps to an integer and keep LRs unchanged. Early steps are cheap and numerous, later steps are larger and less noisy.

title: Grouped-query attention with half the KV heads
spec: Use grouped-query attention where the number of key/value heads is half the number of query heads (each KV head shared by two query heads). This reduces K/V projection parameters and memory bandwidth, freeing time for more steps in the fixed budget.

title: Longer warmdown window
spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the final 70% of the time budget instead of 50%. Keep the linear shape and all other hyperparameters the same.

title: Parallel attention and MLP block
spec: Change each transformer block to the parallel form x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), sharing a single pre-norm for both branches. This reduces sequential kernel launches per layer and may increase throughput within the fixed time budget.

title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown after the constant phase with a cosine decay: multiplier = 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi * p)) where p runs from 0 to 1 across the warmdown window (the last WARMDOWN_RATIO of the time budget). The constant phase and the peak LRs are unchanged.

title: Non-zero final LR fraction
spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the warmdown ends at 10% of each group's peak LR instead of decaying to zero. This keeps some learning signal at the end of the run; no other change.

title: Byte-weighted cross-entropy loss
spec: Since the metric is bits per byte, weight each target token's cross-entropy by its UTF-8 byte length (computed from the tokenizer's decoded string for each vocab id, precomputed once into a float tensor of length vocab_size). Loss = sum(w[target] * ce) / sum(w[target]) over the batch, so the gradient matches the bpb objective instead of per-token averaging. Keep the logged training loss in the same form. Do not change the evaluation call or the summary printing. If the tokenizer's byte lengths are not available through the already-imported names, fall back to weight 1 and skip the change.

title: Hold embedding LR constant through warmdown
spec: Keep the token-embedding and lm_head Adam learning rates at their peak values for the whole run, applying the warmdown multiplier only to the Muon matrix and scalar parameter groups. This makes the warmdown apply only to the parameters that benefit most from annealing.

title: Exponential moving average of weights
spec: Maintain an EMA of model parameters with decay 0.999 updated each optimizer step, and use the EMA weights for the final model state used in evaluation. Keep the training weights unchanged for the optimizer. Do not modify the evaluation call; only swap in the EMA weights before the existing evaluation code runs.

title: Value embeddings injected into later-layer values
spec: Create a second embedding table of the same vocabulary and dimension as the token embedding, initialized to zero. In the second half of the blocks (layers index >= DEPTH/2), add a learnable scalar-gated copy of this embedding of the current token to the value projection output v before attention, i.e. v = v + lambda_l * ve[token], with lambda_l a per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5 and kept in the scalar Adam group. Train the value-embedding table with EMBEDDING_LR in its own Adam group. The rest of attention (RoPE, QK-norm, window pattern) is unchanged.

title: Sandwich norm on sublayer outputs
spec: In each Block, apply an extra RMSNorm to the output of the attention sublayer and to the output of the MLP sublayer before each is added to the residual stream. That is x = x + norm_post_attn(attn(norm_pre(x))) and x = x + norm_post_mlp(mlp(norm_pre(x))), with the post-norms having no learnable weight (or a learnable per-channel gain initialized to 1). Keep the existing pre-norms and the existing residual-scale scalars. This bounds the magnitude each sublayer writes into the residual stream.

title: Tied input and output embeddings with one extra layer
spec: Tie the lm_head weight to the token embedding matrix (single shared parameter, so lm_head = embedding.T), and remove the separate UNEMBEDDING_LR Adam group, folding the shared matrix into the EMBEDDING_LR group. Use the parameters saved by the removed head to increase DEPTH by 1 so the total parameter budget and wall-clock stay roughly constant. Scale the tied embedding init to std 0.02 at start and keep the logit softmax path unchanged. Recompute model_dim from the new DEPTH using ASPECT_RATIO so head count and HEAD_DIM still divide evenly.

title: More conservative Newton-Schulz coefficients in Muon
spec: In the Muon orthogonalization step, replace the quintic Newton-Schulz coefficients with the more conservative set (a, b, c) = (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) that converges to an exact polar factor rather than the aggressive oscillating set currently used. Keep the same number of iterations and the same momentum, LR, and weight decay. The goal is a smoother orthogonalized update that is less sensitive to the 300 s budget's late-training gradient scale.

title: Sequence-length curriculum
spec: Train with a shorter sequence length early and lengthen it later: use half the configured sequence length for the first 30% of the time budget and the full length afterwards. Keep tokens per step at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE by adjusting the number of sequences per micro-batch. The data loader interface stays the same.

title: Shallower and wider model
spec: Set DEPTH to 6 and ASPECT_RATIO to 85 so the model dimension grows to roughly 512 with fewer layers. Keep HEAD_DIM and the rest unchanged. Fewer layers run faster per step, so this tests whether more tokens seen in 300 s outweigh the loss of depth.

title: Exponential moving average of weights
spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Use the averaged parameters for the final model state that the harness evaluates, by copying the EMA weights into the model just before the end-of-training evaluation call. Do not alter the evaluation call itself.

title: Sequence-length curriculum
spec: Train on shorter sequences early and longer ones later: for the first 30 percent of the time budget use half the context length by splitting each batch into two halves along the sequence dimension, then switch to full length. Keep the total tokens per step constant. This increases early step throughput, and the training data loader interface is not to be changed beyond the batch reshape.

title: Head dimension 64
spec: Change HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so each attention layer has twice as many heads of half the width, with the model dimension unchanged. Adjust nothing else. Smaller heads often give better per-parameter attention quality at small scale and may help the short run.

title: Lower scalar LR
spec: Reduce SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 for the per-layer scalar parameters (residual and skip mixing scalars) that use Adam. Leave the matrix, embedding and unembedding learning rates unchanged. Large scalar learning rates can make the residual gains oscillate, so this checks whether a gentler scalar step improves convergence.

title: Larger total batch size
spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 tokens per optimizer step by doubling gradient accumulation with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE fixed at 64. Fewer, less noisy steps may give a better gradient signal per update for Muon. Keep all learning rates unchanged.

title: Muon momentum warmup
spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value each step from the step counter and writing it into the Muon param groups before the optimizer step. Leave all other Muon logic unchanged.

title: Shape-aware Muon LR scaling
spec: Scale the Muon learning rate per matrix by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so that tall matrices (for example MLP up-projections) get a proportionally larger step, rather than using one global MATRIX_LR for all shapes. Compute the factor once per parameter when building the param groups. Keep MATRIX_LR as the base value.

title: Longer warmdown fraction
spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so that the learning rate begins decaying earlier and spends more of the 300 s budget at reduced LR. Keep the linear shape and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0. This tests whether a longer anneal improves the final checkpoint quality.

title: Learned per-head QK temperature
spec: Add one learnable scalar per attention head, initialized to 1.0, that multiplies the query vectors after RoPE, or equivalently scales the attention logits. Put it in the scalar (Adam, SCALAR_LR) parameter group, with no weight decay. Keep the standard 1/sqrt(head_dim) scaling in addition to this factor, so the initial behavior is unchanged. This lets each head learn its own sharpness at negligible cost.

title: Depth 10 with fixed model width
spec: Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10 and set ASPECT_RATIO to 51 so the model dimension stays near 512 (10 times 51 is about 512, rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM). Keep HEAD_DIM, window pattern and all other settings the same. This tests whether extra layers at similar width beat the current shallower model within the fixed time budget.

title: NorMuon: per-row normalization of Muon updates
spec: In the Muon optimizer step, after the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization of each matrix update, divide each output row by its own RMS (or L2 norm), then rescale the whole update so its overall RMS matches the current uniform Muon scaling. Keep the momentum, Nesterov, weight decay and LR schedule unchanged, and apply the change only to the matrix parameters that already use Muon. This equalizes update magnitude across neurons, which the uniform Muon step does not do. Keep the code to a few lines inside the existing Muon update function.

title: Two-phase step decay LR instead of linear warmdown
spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a step schedule: hold the full LR multiplier 1.0 until 60% of the time budget, then drop to 0.2 for the rest of training, applied to all parameter groups. Keep WARMUP_RATIO = 0. This tests whether a long high-LR plateau followed by a sharp drop beats the current continuously decaying schedule. Do not change any other hyperparameter.

title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary loss
spec: Add one auxiliary head that predicts the token two positions ahead from the final hidden state, using a separate linear projection that shares the embedding dimension. Train with total loss = CE(next token) + 0.3 * CE(token at t+2), where the auxiliary term is computed only over valid positions. Use the main lm_head for the primary term unchanged. Drop the auxiliary head at evaluation time so the reported val_bpb uses only the next-token head. This gives an extra training signal per forward pass.

title: Smaller total batch size
spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step, keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the gradient accumulation logic unchanged so that the number of accumulation steps halves. More optimizer steps fit into 300 s, which may help a model that is still improving quickly.

title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown over the last WARMDOWN_RATIO fraction of the time budget with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC times the peak, computed from elapsed time over the budget. Apply the same multiplier to every parameter group. Keep the warmup and budget logic unchanged.

title: Hard-example loss reweighting by top-k token loss
spec: In the training loss, compute per-token cross-entropy for each micro-batch and average over all tokens, but multiply the loss of tokens whose loss is in the top 25 percent of the batch by 1.5 before averaging. Leave the weights for the other tokens at 1.0 and detach the weighting mask so gradients flow only through the loss. Evaluation is unchanged and the reported metric is computed by the harness on the model, not on the training loss. This focuses gradient signal on hard positions, which may help the bits-per-byte metric in a short run. Keep the optimizer and schedule the same.

title: Full attention in every layer
spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "LLLL" so every layer attends over the full context instead of using half-context sliding windows in three of four layers. Keep everything else unchanged. This tests whether the shorter windows are limiting quality at this sequence length.

title: Cosine warmdown shape
spec: Replace the linear warmdown multiplier with a cosine decay: multiplier = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)) where p is the fraction of the warmdown window elapsed, applied to all parameter groups. The warmdown still starts at (1-WARMDOWN_RATIO) of the time budget and ends at zero LR.

title: Non-zero final learning rate
spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.1 so the learning rate floors at 10 percent of its initial value at the end of the warmdown instead of reaching zero. Keep the linear warmdown shape and all other settings unchanged.

title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameter count
spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a SwiGLU block: a gate and an up projection to hidden size round(8/3 * model_dim), then SiLU(gate) times up, then a down projection. Scale the hidden size so the total MLP parameter count matches the current model. Keep the attention and everything else unchanged.

title: Shape-matched RMS scaling for Muon updates
spec: Replace the Muon per-matrix LR scale factor sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) with a match-RMS scale of 0.2*sqrt(max(rows, cols)) applied to the orthogonalized update. This lets the Muon matrices share a similar effective LR with the Adam-trained parameters. Retune MATRIX_LR is not needed for the first test, so keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04 and adjust only the scale expression.

title: Progressive sequence length
spec: Train with a shorter sequence length of 512 tokens for the first 40 percent of the time budget and switch to the full sequence length afterwards, increasing the batch row count so tokens per step stay at TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE. Keep learning rates unchanged. Short sequences early give cheaper steps and more updates.

title: Deeper narrower model
spec: Set DEPTH from 8 to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48 so model_dim stays near 512 while adding two layers. Keep HEAD_DIM, learning rates and all other settings unchanged. This tests whether extra depth helps within the fixed time budget.

title: Smaller total batch size
spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each optimizer step covers about 262K tokens. Keep the learning rates the same. This doubles the number of optimizer steps in the fixed wall-clock budget, which may help more than the reduced gradient quality.

title: Longer warmdown phase
spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the final 70 percent of the time budget instead of the final 50 percent. Keep the linear shape and all other settings as they are.

title: Auxiliary multi-token prediction head
spec: Add a second prediction target that predicts the token two positions ahead. Reuse the existing lm_head on the final hidden states shifted by one extra position, and compute a cross-entropy loss for that target. Add it to the main loss with weight 0.1. Use only the main head at evaluation time, so the evaluation path is unchanged. This adds a denser training signal per forward pass at a small extra compute cost.

title: Short linear warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.02 and use a linear ramp from 0 to 1 over the first 2 percent of the time budget for all parameter groups. This avoids a large initial update when Muon and high-LR Adam groups start, while still leaving most of the budget at full LR.

title: ResFormer-style value residual
spec: Save the value projection output of the first attention layer and add a learned per-layer mixing of it into the value of each later attention layer, v_l = v_l + lambda_l * v_0, with lambda_l initialized to zero. Use one scalar per layer added to the existing scalar parameters. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Muon momentum warmup
spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to the current 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold it at 0.95. Implement by computing the momentum value each step from the step counter and writing it into the Muon param-group dict before the update. No other changes.

title: Linearly decayed weight decay
spec: Scale the Muon weight decay (currently 0.2) by a factor that decreases linearly from 1.0 at the start of training to 0.0 at the end, computed from elapsed time over the time budget. Apply the factor each step to the decay term only. This keeps regularization strong early and lets the final weights fit the data.

title: Tail averaging of weights over the last 20 percent of training
spec: Maintain a running uniform average of the model parameters, starting once elapsed training time passes 80 percent of the TIME budget and updating after every optimizer step. Keep the average in a separate buffer that is not used for gradient updates. At the end of training, copy the averaged weights into the model before the final evaluation call, leaving the evaluation function itself unchanged. The average smooths the noisy final iterates produced by the Muon steps during the decay phase.

title: Compile with max-autotune kernels
spec: Change the model compile call to torch.compile(model, mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', dynamic=False), keeping the same inputs, batch shapes, and everything else unchanged. Autotuning runs during startup, which is not counted against the 300 s training budget, but the total startup plus training must stay under 450 s, so check the startup time in the log. The goal is to get more optimizer steps in the fixed wall-clock budget from faster fused matmul and attention kernels. Do not change any evaluation code.

title: Per-layer learned residual scaling
spec: Add one learnable scalar per block that multiplies the attention and MLP branch outputs before they are added to the residual stream, initialized to 1.0 and trained with SCALAR_LR. This lets the model learn how much each layer contributes. Keep the number of added parameters negligible.

title: Decoupled weight decay on embeddings and lm_head
spec: Add a small decoupled weight decay (0.01 times the LR, AdamW style) to the Adam-optimized embedding and lm_head parameters, which currently receive none. Apply it inside the Adam step as p.mul_(1 - lr*wd) before the gradient update. Keep the scalar parameters without decay.

title: Weight averaging over final training window
spec: During the last 20 percent of the time budget, accumulate a running uniform average of model parameters taken every 50 steps. Before final evaluation, copy the averaged weights into the model. This approximates checkpoint averaging and often smooths the end of a warmdown. Keep the training loop otherwise unchanged.

title: Muon momentum warmup
spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by updating the momentum value in the Muon param-group dict each step before the optimizer step. Leave all other Muon settings unchanged.

title: Logit z-loss regularization
spec: Add an auxiliary loss 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits, dim=-1)^2) to the cross-entropy loss to keep output logits from drifting in scale. Compute it on the same logits used for the main loss, in float32. Leave all other training code unchanged.

title: Short warmup before warmdown
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the learning rate ramps linearly from 0 over the first 2 percent of the time budget before the existing warmdown begins. This guards against early instability at the high embedding and scalar learning rates. Only the warmup constant changes, plus confirming the schedule function handles a nonzero warmup.

title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary head
spec: Add one extra linear head (shape model_dim x vocab) that predicts the token two positions ahead, reusing the final hidden states. Training loss = CE(next token) + 0.1 * CE(token t+2), with the t+2 targets built by shifting the target tensor by one more position and masking the last position. Use only the next-token head at evaluation and do not change the evaluation call. The auxiliary head is trained with the Adam group used for lm_head.

title: Smaller total batch for more steps
spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each optimizer step covers half as many tokens and more steps occur within the 300 s budget. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the gradient accumulation logic consistent so the accumulation count is recomputed correctly. Single-constant change.

title: Gradient clipping
spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after the backward pass and before the optimizer step, using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over all trainable parameters. This prevents occasional spikes from destabilizing the high learning rates. Do not change any learning rate.

title: Sequence length curriculum
spec: Train on shorter sequences early and grow to the full context length: use half the context length for the first 30 percent of the time budget, then the full length. Keep the number of tokens per optimizer step fixed by adjusting the batch size in sequences so TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE is unchanged. Recompile or reset attention masks at the switch point as needed.

title: Muon Newton-Schulz steps 5 to 3
spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside the Muon update from 5 to 3. This makes each optimizer step cheaper so more steps fit in the fixed 300 s budget. Keep the quintic coefficients and everything else as they are. Compare throughput and final val_bpb against baseline.

title: Cross-layer KV sharing in attention pairs
spec: In the attention blocks, make every odd-indexed layer reuse the key and value projections of the layer directly before it (c_k and c_v are not created for odd layers, so the layer only has its own query and output projections). Keep RoPE and QK-norm as they are. This cuts attention parameters by about a quarter, and the saved parameter budget can be spent on the same width, which should give more steps in 300 s.

title: Exponential moving average of weights for evaluation
spec: Maintain an EMA copy of model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Run the final evaluation with the EMA weights swapped in. Do not modify the evaluation call itself; only swap parameter values before the evaluation runs, and keep the live training weights unchanged.

title: Smaller batch for more optimizer steps
spec: Lower TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each step uses half as many tokens and the 300 s budget yields roughly twice as many optimizer updates. Keep the LRs unchanged and make sure gradient accumulation still divides cleanly by DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE.

title: Cosine warmdown shape
spec: Replace the linear time-based warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO of the budget. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5 and the same peak LRs.

title: Weight decay linearly annealed to zero
spec: Scale the effective weight decay linearly from WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 at the start to 0.0 at the end of the time budget, tracking the elapsed-time fraction used by the LR schedule. Apply this to the Muon and any other decayed parameter groups.

title: Weight decay on Muon without cautious mask
spec: Replace the cautious (sign-agreement masked) weight decay in Muon with standard decoupled weight decay applied to every matrix update, using WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 scaled by the current LR. Keep the rest of the Muon update unchanged.

title: Bigram hash embedding
spec: Add a small hashed bigram embedding table, indexed by hash(previous token, current token) modulo a table size such as 4096, and add its output to the token embedding with a learned scalar initialized at zero. Keep the main embedding dimension unchanged.

title: Shallower, wider model
spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 85 so the width grows while depth shrinks, aiming for more throughput per step within the 300 s budget. Keep HEAD_DIM = 128 and the other settings unchanged.

title: Warmdown ratio 0.7
spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the final 70% of the time budget instead of 50%. Keep the linear warmdown shape and FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0.

title: Short linear warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from zero over the first 2% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. Everything else stays the same.

title: Full attention in every layer pattern change
spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSLL" so two of the four blocks use full context, testing whether more global attention layers help more than the extra compute costs. Keep all other settings.

title: Value embeddings (ResFormer style)
spec: Add a learned per-layer gate that mixes the first layer's attention value vectors into the value projection of later layers, with the mixing weight initialized to zero. This adds little compute and no extra sequence-length cost.

title: Weight EMA for evaluation
spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step, and use the EMA weights for the final evaluation call. Do not alter the evaluation call itself; only swap the parameter values used by the model before the existing eval runs.

title: Global gradient-norm clipping
spec: Before each optimizer step, call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over all trainable parameters with max_norm=1.0 and keep the rest of the loop unchanged. Gradients are clipped per step, which guards against occasional loss spikes at the high embedding and scalar learning rates (EMBEDDING_LR 0.6, SCALAR_LR 0.5) and could allow a more aggressive step size. Log nothing new; the metric path is untouched.

title: Logit z-loss
spec: Add a z-loss term of 1e-4 times the mean squared log-sum-exp of the output logits to the training loss to keep logits from drifting in scale. Apply it only to the training loss, not the evaluation.

title: Gradient norm clipping
spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after the backward pass and before optimizer steps, using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over all trainable parameters. This guards against loss spikes at the high embedding and scalar LRs.

title: Lower beta1 for Adam groups
spec: Set the Adam beta1 for the embedding, lm_head, and scalar groups to 0.9 while keeping beta2 at 0.95. This makes Adam react faster to gradient changes over the short 300 s run. Muon is unaffected.

title: QK-norm with learnable per-head gain
spec: Normalize queries and keys with RMSNorm over the head dimension before rotary embeddings, and add a learnable per-head scalar gain on the query side initialized to 1. This stabilizes attention logits at high LR.

title: Deeper and narrower model
spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 52 so model_dim stays near 512 with 25% more layers. Keep HEAD_DIM, WINDOW_PATTERN, and all other settings unchanged. Tests whether extra depth helps more than the lost width.

title: Larger total batch size
spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**20 (about 1M tokens per optimizer step), which increases gradient accuracy at the cost of fewer steps. Keep the LRs unchanged for the first test and let gradient accumulation increase to match.

title: Short linear warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so that all LR groups ramp linearly from 0 to their peak over the first 3% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. The current schedule starts at full LR immediately, and this tests whether a brief ramp stabilizes early Muon updates.

title: Separate warmdown for Muon and Adam groups
spec: Keep the Adam-style groups (embedding, lm_head, scalars) on the current linear warmdown that starts at 50% of the budget. For the Muon matrix group only, begin the warmdown later, at 70% of the budget, and decay it to 0 by the end, so the matrix parameters keep learning at full rate for longer. Compute the two multipliers from elapsed time fraction as separate functions, and apply them to their respective param groups each step.

title: Weight EMA for evaluation
spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model weights with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Run the final model evaluation with the EMA weights swapped in. Training dynamics are unchanged. The evaluation call itself is not modified.

title: SwiGLU MLP
spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU MLP. Use a hidden width of about 8/3 times model_dim, rounded to a multiple of 64, so the parameter count stays close to the current MLP. Keep the rest of the block unchanged.

title: ResFormer-style first-layer value residual
spec: Capture the value projection v from layer 0 and, in every later attention layer, mix it into the current value as v_l = lambda_l * v_l + (1 - lambda_l) * v_0, where lambda_l is a learnable per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5 and trained with SCALAR_LR. Layer 0 is unchanged. The extra cost is one elementwise blend per layer, with no new matmuls. Keep the sliding-window pattern and rotary embeddings as they are.

title: Shape-aware Muon update scaling
spec: Scale each Muon matrix update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) so that tall and wide matrices get comparable update RMS, instead of the current unscaled orthogonalized update. Apply it in the Muon step right after orthogonalization and keep MATRIX_LR at 0.04 for the first test.

title: Light decoupled weight decay on Adam parameters
spec: Add decoupled weight decay of 0.01 (scaled by the current LR multiplier) to the AdamW-managed groups: token embeddings, lm_head, and per-layer scalars. Currently these groups get no decay. Muon's WEIGHT_DECAY=0.2 stays as is.

title: Ramped Muon weight decay
spec: Set the Muon weight decay to 0 at the start and increase it linearly to WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.2 by 60% of the time budget, then hold it constant. Early in training the weights should move freely, and later decay acts as a regularizer that shrinks the weights toward the constrained norm. Update the decay value of the Muon param group at each step from the elapsed time fraction. Leave the Adam groups and the rest of the schedule unchanged.

title: Higher Muon matrix LR
spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 for the Muon matrix parameters, keeping the Adam LRs unchanged. This probes whether the Muon group is under-driven in the short time budget.

title: Longer warmdown
spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the last 70% of the 300 s budget. Keep the peak LRs, warmup (0), and FINAL_LR_FRAC (0) unchanged. This is a single-constant change.

title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
spec: Replace the linear LR warmdown with a cosine decay from the peak LR to zero over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO fraction of the time budget. Keep the warmup and the peak LRs unchanged. The LR multiplier is a function of elapsed time over the budget.

title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear
spec: Replace the linear warmdown in the LR schedule with a cosine decay that goes from full LR at the start of the warmdown phase (WARMDOWN_RATIO of the budget before the end) to FINAL_LR_FRAC at the end. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups.

title: Value residual from first layer
spec: Pass the value projection of the first layer forward and mix it into every later layer's values with a learned per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5. Specifically, v_l = a_l * v_l + (1 - a_l) * v_0 for layers after the first. Adds only a few scalar parameters.

title: Z-loss on logits
spec: Add an auxiliary loss of 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training cross-entropy to keep the output logit scale stable. Do not add it to the validation loss path. This is a light regularizer on the unembedding.

title: Deeper and narrower model
spec: Set DEPTH from 8 to 10 and reduce ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 52 so model_dim stays close to the incumbent's cost, favoring depth over width. Keep HEAD_DIM at 128 so the head count adjusts. Check that DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 still fits in 40 GB.

title: Sqrt-shaped warmdown
spec: Use a warmdown multiplier of sqrt(remaining_fraction) during the final WARMDOWN_RATIO of training, where remaining_fraction goes from 1 to 0 across that phase. This decays the LR more slowly at first and faster near the end than linear. Apply to all groups.

title: Smaller head dimension
spec: Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64, which doubles the number of attention heads at the same model_dim. More heads with smaller dimension can capture more diverse attention patterns in a small model. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Sequence length curriculum
spec: Start training at half the sequence length used by the incumbent and switch to the full sequence length at 50% of the time budget, keeping the same tokens per step by adjusting the batch dimension. Rotary embeddings and masks must handle the change. This speeds early steps and ends at full context.

title: Separate warmdown fraction per optimizer group
spec: Keep the linear warmdown for Muon matrix parameters as it is now, which starts at WARMDOWN_RATIO of the budget. For the Adam groups (embeddings, lm_head, and scalars), start a faster linear warmdown earlier, at 0.3 of the time budget, so those groups reach zero LR before the matrices do. Compute each group's LR multiplier from elapsed time fraction separately, and keep the final LR fraction at zero for all groups.

title: Weight EMA for evaluation
spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters with decay 0.999 updated after each optimizer step, and evaluate the EMA weights at the end of training instead of the raw weights. Store the EMA copy in the same dtype. Do not change the evaluation call or the summary printing; only swap the weights before the existing evaluation call.

title: Grouped-query attention with half the KV heads
spec: Set the number of key/value heads to n_head // 2 while keeping n_head and HEAD_DIM unchanged. Repeat each K and V head across its paired query heads before attention (for example with repeat_interleave), so the attention call and its shapes stay the same. Keep all other hyperparameters fixed. The goal is fewer K/V projection parameters and cheaper attention, which gives more optimizer steps within the 300 s budget.

title: Auxiliary multi-token prediction head
spec: Add one extra prediction head that predicts the token two steps ahead from the final hidden state (shift targets by 2, shared lm_head weights with a separate small linear adapter of shape model_dim x model_dim, zero-initialized). Training loss is the standard next-token cross-entropy plus 0.1 times the t+2 cross-entropy, computed on the valid positions only. The primary logits used for the reported model output remain the t+1 head only, so evaluation is unaffected. Drop the auxiliary term at the start of the warmdown so the final objective matches the metric.

title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameter count
spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU block: a gate projection and an up projection from model_dim to hidden, then silu(gate) * up, then a down projection back to model_dim. Set hidden to roughly 2/3 of the current MLP width (about 8/3 * model_dim) so the total parameter count matches the baseline. Keep the same Muon and Adam parameter grouping, with all three matrices in the Muon group.

title: Sequence-length curriculum
spec: Train with shorter sequences in the first 30 percent of the time budget, for example half the usual context length with twice the batch in sequences, then switch to full context for the rest. Keep the tokens per optimizer step identical. This may speed early learning and reduces attention cost early on.

title: Muon learning-rate sweep (lower)
spec: Change only MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.025. Keep every other hyperparameter, including the warmdown schedule and WEIGHT_DECAY, identical so the result isolates the matrix learning rate.

title: Final LR floor at 10 percent
spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the warmdown ends at 10 percent of the peak learning rate rather than at zero. Keep all other schedule settings unchanged. This checks whether a nonzero final LR helps the last steps on this short run.

title: Previous-token bigram mixing at input
spec: After the token embedding, add a learned gate-weighted copy of the previous token's embedding to each position, with the first position receiving no addition. Use a single learnable scalar gate initialized near zero so the model starts close to the baseline. This gives cheap local context at the input.

title: Weight decay sweep
spec: Change only WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 for the Muon matrix parameters. Keep all learning rates and schedules identical so the effect of decay strength on the 300 s run can be read directly.

title: Deeper, narrower model
spec: Set DEPTH from 8 to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 48 so the model width stays near 480 while the layer count increases. Keep HEAD_DIM and all optimizer settings as they are. This trades width for depth under the same time budget.

title: Sliding window pattern all full attention
spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN to full-context attention on every layer (for example "LLLL"-style behavior for all DEPTH layers). The sequences are short enough that the half-context sliding layers may be losing useful context, and removing them might lower validation bpb even if each step is slightly slower.

title: Smaller total batch for more steps
spec: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each optimizer step uses about 262K tokens. Under a fixed 300 s clock this gives roughly twice as many optimizer steps, which may matter more than per-step gradient quality for a small model. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the gradient accumulation logic consistent with the new total.

title: Exponential moving average of weights
spec: Maintain an EMA of all trainable parameters with decay 0.999 updated every step. Evaluate using the EMA weights at the end of training by swapping them in before the harness evaluation path runs. Do not alter the evaluation call or summary printing; only swap the parameter values beforehand.

title: Global gradient-norm clipping
spec: Before each optimizer step, clip the global gradient norm across all trainable parameters to 1.0 using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_. Apply it after backward and before the Muon and Adam steps. This adds no new hyperparameter beyond the threshold constant. It guards against the occasional large-gradient spikes that high LRs such as EMBEDDING_LR=0.6 can produce.

title: Head dimension 64
spec: Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64 so each attention layer has twice as many heads at the same model width. Keep the model dimension unchanged. This tests whether finer-grained heads help at this small scale.

title: Larger total batch
spec: Double TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 so each step uses about 1M tokens. Keep the learning rates unchanged and let the existing gradient accumulation absorb the larger batch. This tests the opposite trade-off, lower gradient noise at fewer steps.

title: Muon update shape scaling (Moonlight-style)
spec: Scale each Muon orthogonalized update by 0.2 * sqrt(max(rows, cols)) instead of the current shape factor, so the update RMS matches AdamW's typical magnitude and one shared learning rate transfers across matrix shapes. Retune nothing else; keep MATRIX_LR as the base learning rate.

title: Value residual from first layer
spec: In CausalSelfAttention.forward, save the value tensor v produced by the first transformer block and, in every later block, replace v with (1 - lam) * v + lam * v_first, where lam is a new per-layer learnable scalar initialized to 0.5 and kept in the scalar Adam group (SCALAR_LR). Leave the first block unchanged. No other hyperparameters change. This is the ResFormer-style value residual that lets deeper layers reuse first-layer value features.

title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameter count
spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP in each block with a SwiGLU MLP. Use a gate projection and an up projection, each mapping model_dim to hidden size round(8/3 * model_dim) rounded to a multiple of 64, followed by SiLU(gate) times up, then the down projection back to model_dim. This keeps the parameter count roughly equal to the existing 4x MLP. Keep the Muon grouping rule so all new matrices are still orthogonalized.

title: Looped shared-weight block recurrence
spec: Keep the total number of block applications at DEPTH but store only DEPTH//2 distinct transformer blocks. The forward pass applies the block list twice in sequence, with the second pass using the same weights and a learned per-pass scalar gate initialized to 1 on the residual branch. Optimizer parameter groups should deduplicate the shared tensors so each is updated once. Widen model_dim by about 1.2x (keeping HEAD_DIM) to use the freed parameters. This is a bolder test of whether compute per parameter beats parameter count under a fixed time budget.

title: Warmdown length extension
spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the linear LR decay covers the last 70 percent of the time budget. Keep the warmup at zero and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0. This tests whether a longer anneal to zero improves the final validation loss.

title: Deeper and narrower model
spec: Set DEPTH to 10 and reduce ASPECT_RATIO to 48 so model_dim is about 480, rounding it to a multiple of HEAD_DIM. More layers can improve quality per parameter at similar cost. Confirm WINDOW_PATTERN still applies cleanly to the new depth.

title: Longer warmdown ratio
spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays over the final 70% of the time budget. The LR still ends at FINAL_LR_FRAC. This shifts more of the run into the low-LR regime that usually gives the best final loss.

title: Full attention window pattern
spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'LLLL' so every layer uses full context. At this sequence length the sliding windows may save little time while removing some context, so this checks whether full attention improves the bits-per-byte score per token.

title: Larger total batch
spec: Double TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 by increasing gradient accumulation steps, keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64. Each step averages more tokens, which can give smoother gradients for Muon at the cost of fewer updates. Re-check that the time budget still fits.

title: Lion for embedding table
spec: Replace the Adam optimizer for the token embedding parameters with Lion (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.99, sign-based update), using an LR about 3x smaller than EMBEDDING_LR (roughly 0.1-0.2). Keep Adam for the other non-matrix groups and Muon for the matrices.

title: Compile mode tuning
spec: Change the torch.compile call to use mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' or dynamic=False, whichever gives higher steps per second on the A100 in a quick check. The goal is more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s window without changing the model math.

title: Smaller total batch for more steps
spec: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 tokens per optimizer step. At a fixed 300 s budget this doubles the number of updates, which often helps small models that are not compute-bound. Adjust gradient accumulation so DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE stays 64.

title: Higher Muon matrix LR
spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 while keeping the same warmdown schedule. Muon with orthogonalized updates often tolerates larger LRs, so this probes whether the current value is under-tuned for this short run.

title: Sequence-length curriculum
spec: Train with a shorter context for the first 30% of the time budget (for example half the sequence length, with the batch reshaped to keep the same token count per step), then switch to full context. Shorter sequences early give cheaper steps and faster initial loss reduction. Implement by reshaping the existing batch tensors without touching the data loader or the eval path.

title: Cosine warmdown shape
spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine curve over the warmdown window, going from the peak LR to FINAL_LR_FRAC times the peak. Use lr_mult = final + 0.5*(1-final)*(1+cos(pi*t)) with t from 0 to 1 across the warmdown. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5.

title: Zero weight decay on embeddings and norms
spec: Exclude the token embedding, lm_head, and all norm/scalar parameters from decoupled weight decay. Apply WEIGHT_DECAY only to the Muon matrix parameters, as now. Implement by setting weight_decay=0 in the Adam parameter groups.

title: Sigmoid output gate per attention head
spec: After scaled-dot-product attention, multiply each head's output by a learned sigmoid gate computed from the layer's normalized input, g = sigmoid(x @ W_g) with W_g a new Linear(model_dim, n_heads) initialized to zero so the gate starts at 0.5. Apply the gate per head before the output projection. This adds a small number of parameters per layer and gives the model a learned way to suppress or pass each head, as in recent gated-attention work. Do not change the optimizer grouping beyond placing W_g with the other matrix parameters for Muon.

title: Batch-size ramp from 2^18 to 2^19 tokens
spec: Start training with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 for the first 30% of the 300 s time budget, then switch to 2**19 for the remainder. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and sequence length unchanged, and recompute gradient accumulation steps from the current total batch each time it changes (the gradient-accumulation loop already exists, so only the target count varies). Scale the LR schedule position by elapsed time as before and leave Muon and Adam LRs unchanged. The goal is more optimizer steps early, when loss drops fastest, without giving up the larger batch later.

title: Exponential moving average of weights
spec: Maintain an EMA copy of the trainable parameters with decay 0.999 updated after every optimizer step. Before the final training step ends, copy the EMA weights into the live model parameters so the harness evaluates the averaged model. Do not change the evaluation call itself.

title: Short linear warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the LR ramps linearly from 0 over the first 2% of the time budget before the existing schedule takes over. This avoids instability from the very large initial LRs on the embedding and scalar groups.

title: Non-zero final LR fraction

title: Byte-weighted cross-entropy to match the bits-per-byte metric

spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SA', which allows a simpler attention pattern that may be more robust for small models and reduce the overhead of sliding window attention.

title: Decouple Weight Decay from Matrix LR
spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.05 while maintaining a higher MATRIX_LR (e.g., 0.08) to reduce regularization while keeping parameter update momentum.

title: Add gradient clipping
spec: Insert code to clip averaged gradients by a norm of 1.0 if not present, preventing explosion.

title: Increase WARMUP_RATIO to 0.05
spec: Increase WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05 to ramp up the learning rate early, potentially overcoming difficult initial samples in the dataset.

title: Reduce number of iterations
spec: If task allows, reduce the number of epochs required to converge slightly by increasing tokens per batch.

title: Increase matrix learning rate
spec: Increase MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.1 to allow faster convergence of core model parameters.

title: ReLU^2 MLP to SwiGLU
