title: Weight decay 0.1
spec: Reduce WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1 since the training run is short.

title: Gradient clipping at 1.0
spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before the optimizer step to stabilize at higher LRs.

title: Muon momentum warmup shorter/higher
spec: Set Muon momentum final value to 0.97 (from 0.95) and reach it over the first 150 steps if a momentum ramp exists.

title: Longer warmdown ratio 0.7
spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 to test a longer decay phase.

title: Shorter warmdown ratio 0.3
spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 so more time is spent at full LR.

title: Time-based LR schedule with progress floor
spec: Make the schedule use the progress = elapsed_training_time / 300 consistently, and exclude the first 2 steps (compile warmup) from the elapsed time to maximize usable training steps.

title: Depth 6 wider-per-time
spec: Set DEPTH = 6 with ASPECT_RATIO = 96 (model_dim 576, multiple of HEAD_DIM 128 requires 640 -> use ASPECT_RATIO 107 or round dim to 640). Smaller models see more tokens in 300s; keep dim a multiple of HEAD_DIM.

title: Matrix LR 0.05
spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05.

title: Short warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to soften the initial steps, especially useful with Muon and a high embedding LR.

title: Depth 10
spec: Set DEPTH = 10 with ASPECT_RATIO = 64 (dim 640). Check whether the extra capacity compensates for fewer steps; reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 if memory is an issue.

title: Head dim 64
spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 giving more attention heads at the same width.

title: Zero-init lm_head and higher unembedding LR
spec: Initialize lm_head weights to zeros and set UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.008. Zero init of the output projection is common for stability and lets a higher LR be used. Keep logit softcap as is.

title: Batch ramp: small batch early then 2**19
spec: Use gradient accumulation count that depends on training progress: for the first 30% of the time budget use TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**17 (2 micro-steps of 64x2048 tokens), afterward 2**19 (4 micro-steps... use the number needed to reach 2**19). Scale the loss by the current accumulation count so gradients are averaged correctly. Early small batches give many cheap steps when the loss falls fastest.

title: Batch 2**18 with device batch 64
spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 so grad accumulation halves (device batch stays 64). In a fixed 300 s run, more optimizer steps usually help a small model. Keep LRs unchanged. If the code scales anything by batch size, leave it as is.

title: Window pattern SSSSL-like with shorter windows
spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSL" -> fewer full-attention layers; faster steps. Ensure last layer remains full attention.

title: Weight tying-free zero-init lm_head with unembedding LR 0.008
spec: Initialize lm_head weight to zeros (instead of the current small normal init) and raise UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008. Zero-init output heads give clean initial logits and tolerate a higher LR.

title: Change AdamW factor to 1.5
spec: Set AdamW factor to 1.5 to tune the update rule.

title: Add warmup scheduler type
spec: Select a different warmup schedule type to adjust the learning rate curve.

title: Use Adam optimizer
spec: Select Adam as the base optimizer for the matrix layer to potentially improve convergence.

title: Add small weight decay to matrix
spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 1.0 to potentially regularize parameters and reduce earlier overfitting in the validation set.

title: Increase context window granularity
spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SLSS', allowing the sliding window to occupy two consecutive layers more often, which reduces effective token count per step.

title: Larger Muon momentum / longer ramp
spec: In the Muon optimizer setup and its momentum schedule, raise the final momentum from 0.95 to 0.97 (and the ramp target accordingly). Change only the numbers in the existing momentum schedule function. This tests smoother updates late in training.

title: Bolder: Dropout-free label smoothing
spec: In the training loss only (not the evaluation path), replace F.cross_entropy(...) with F.cross_entropy(..., label_smoothing=0.02) in the model forward when targets are given and the model is in training mode (self.training). Make sure the evaluation function still gets the plain loss, by gating on self.training. If the forward cannot distinguish train from eval, skip it.

title: Bolder: Full-attention-only with shorter windows
spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to 'SSSS' with the final layer forced to be long (the code usually forces the last layer to full context already). Short windows are cheaper, so more steps fit in 300s. Only the constant changes. Do not use SLSS, which hurt.

title: Add small warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 so the first ~9s ramp the LR linearly from 0. This may stabilize the high 0.6 embedding LR and the Muon matrix LR early on. Single-constant change.

title: Shorter warmdown with nonzero floor
spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3 and FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.05 so more of the 300s budget trains at full learning rate while the final steps still anneal. Only the two constants change.

title: Smaller model, more steps: DEPTH 6
spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim = 6*64 = 384; with HEAD_DIM 128 this gives 3 heads). Throughput rises, so more tokens are seen in 300s. If the dim is not divisible by HEAD_DIM, set ASPECT_RATIO = 85 so dim is 510 rounded to a multiple of 128 (512). Check that the code handles this.

title: Raise UNEMBEDDING_LR
spec: Set UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.008 (from 0.004) to let the lm_head learn faster in the short budget. Single-constant change.

title: Bolder: wider shallower model with larger aspect ratio
spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 96 (model_dim 576, a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128 is 640 if rounding applies; follow the existing rounding). This tests a wider, shallower shape at a similar parameter count with faster steps. If VRAM overflows, set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32; gradient accumulation should compensate.

title: Lower embedding LR
spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR = 0.3 (from 0.6). The token embedding Adam LR is probably too high for the short run. Single-constant change.

title: Halve total batch size to 2**18
spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation drops from 8 to 4 micro-steps). In a fixed 300s budget this gives about twice as many optimizer steps, which usually helps a small model that is under-trained. Optionally scale MATRIX_LR by about 0.8 if the code does not already adjust it.

title: Bolder: add small dropout-free z-loss
spec: In the training loss computation, add a z-loss term 1e-4 * (logsumexp(logits.float(), dim=-1)**2).mean() to the cross-entropy, only when computing the training loss (not in evaluation, which must stay unaltered). This regularizes logit magnitude and may stabilize the short run. Keep the code to a few lines.

title: Reduce ASPECT_RATIO
spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO = 32 to reduce model width, allowing larger batch size per step.

title: Warmup Schedule
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.1 to add a learning rate warmup phase, stabilizing early training updates.

title: AdamW Weight Decay
spec: Increase WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.5 to reduce overfitting on small models.

title: Add Gradient Clipping
spec: Add gradient clipping to the max to prevent gradient explosions during training.

title: Reduce Warmdown
spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 to end the effective learning rate schedule sooner, allowing better use of the remaining 300s.

title: Warmdown Schedule
spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.1 to gradually reduce learning rate after the warmup phase, preventing gradient explosions.

title: Local Gradient Coarse Graining
spec: Replace total batch size with device batch size of 32 and 5x microbatches in train.step_n to smooth gradients.

title: Reduce Final LR Fraction
spec: Decrease FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.5 to shift more learning rate towards the start of training.

title: GELU Replace
spec: Replace GELU with SiLU activation in GELUSHIFT to improve generalization on small models.

title: Add Gradient Checkpointing
spec: Add gradient checkpointing to reduce memory usage and allow larger batch sizes.

title: Reduce Weight Decay
spec: Decrease WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.01 to avoid regularization noise on larger batch sizes.

title: Add Normalization
spec: Add layer normalization in the transformer layer to stabilize training.

title: Micro-Batch Scheduled Warmup
spec: Instead of warmup on the full batch, split the batch into micro-batches and apply a warmup schedule that gradually increases the effective learning rate for those micro-batches, allowing the model to adapt faster and reduce val_bpb.

title: Reduce Momentum
spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.85, 0.999) to reduce momentum, reducing oscillation for faster initial convergence.

title: GradClip along Batch Dimensions
spec: Replace global gradient norm clipping with a batch-dimension clip: clip the norm of the gradient tensor along batch dimensions (batchwise grad clipping) before averaging. This stabilizes training when microbatches differ significantly in loss contribution.

title: Residual-in-Residual Blocks (RRDB) with Skip Connections
spec: Modify the transformer core to add a secondary residual connection in each layer: the layer output $x'$ is computed as $y' = (ResidualBlock(x) + x) * norm_scale$. This doubles the effective expressiveness per layer at minimal overhead, allowing larger effective batch sizes without OOM.

title: Optimal Reg
spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.08 and add a separate regularization term for per-layer scalars that decays 1e-4 times faster than matrix regularization; this reduces gradient noise.

title: Linear Warmup Schedule
spec: Replace WARMUP_RATIO=0.0 with WARMUP_STEPS becalculated from time_budget so that warmup covers 0-10% of steps, then slope rises to MATRIX_LR over 2000 more steps. This often stabilizes early gradient flows.

title: Wavenumber LR
spec: Apply a wavenumber learning rate to each layer: 0.85 * MATRIX_LR for odd layers and 0.95 * MATRIX_LR for even layers. reduces noise propagation.

title: Layer-wise Learning Rate Sweep
spec: Introduce LRSCHEDULES variable mapping layer index to a ratio of MATRIX_LR. Layers 0-4 use 0.4*LR, layers 5-8 use 0.8*LR. Applies a gentle LR drop to early layers to reduce noise propagation.

title: Residual Mixing 3
spec: Replace 1.0+residual with 1.3+residual; this modifies the linear combination to be 1.3 * prev_output + input, which can smooth gradient flow by 2.1%.

title: Clock-Locked LR
spec: Switch to a clock-based LR schedule: start at MATRIX_LR and decay to 10% of that over 60 seconds, then stay flat until 30s before final 10s with a steep linear sink to 0.01 of MATRIX_LR. This avoids entropy-based scheduling noise.

title: Differential Dropout
spec: Replace standard dropout with a dropout mask that varies with the global sequence position within a batch (sinusoird mask) so that different sequence positions see different dropout patterns, promoting frequency-domain smoothing.

title: Optimal Epoch Divisor
spec: Divide TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE training steps by a divisor-of-2^19, p=1 as a starting point; this allows dynamic scheduling of batches to fit wall-clock time.

title: Lambda Constraints
spec: Add lambda constraints to the loss: a small penalty on the sum of squared activations for the first three layers, scaled by 4.1e-6.

title: Adaptive Time-Dependent LR
spec: Replace the static warmup/schedule with a lightweight logistic-sigmoid function of global step that acts as the single 'learning rate' applied to all optimizer groups, allowing the entire model to ramp down together in a smoother, non-linear decay curve.

title: Optimal Regen Winnow
spec: Apply a non-linear soft-thresholding (ReLU-style) winnowing mechanism to the residual stream's coefficients before mixing, as opposed to simple passing, to suppress vanishingly small activations that contribute little to the loss gradient.

title: Stochastic Depth
spec: Insert a stochastic depth gate: with probability 0.2, skip the residual connection for the first 200s. This can smooth the gradient flow.

title: Quasi-Residual Mixing
spec: Replace residual connection with a 'q-residual' that mixes 30% of input before summing with prev output. This reduces pathological residual gradients in the first few epochs.

title: Residual Stream Compression
spec: Apply a soft-shrinkage (soft threshold) to the residual stream before it is added to the inputs, using a lambda that scales with the layer depth. This forces residuals of small magnitude to zero, effectively performing aggressive pruning on each layer.

title: Cross-Attention Feature Fusion
spec: Insert a small cross-attention block between the residual and x0 components of each transformer layer. This block uses the residual as the query and the x0 component as the key/value. The output is fused back into the residual stream, allowing the model to dynamically learn correlations between its own outputs and internal parameters.

title: Layer-wise Regularization
spec: Add a regularization term to the loss that penalizes the difference between the weight distribution of each layer and a Gaussian distribution. The penalty is scaled by the layer index, forcing early layers to be more regularized while allowing later layers to vary more freely.

title: Arch Scale-RF
spec: Increase DEPTH to 12 while keeping ASPECT_RATIO at 64; this changes model_dim to 768, raising compute density but also additive regularization from wider heads, reducing jitter.

title: Temporal Order Mixing
spec: Before applying the attention mechanism, replace each position's query vector with a weighted combination of its left and right context tokens' queries, using a ratio that decays exponentially with distance. This allows the model to learn attention patterns over spatial neighborhoods rather than single positions.

title: Lower total batch to 2**18
spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation halves). In a fixed 300 s budget with a small model, more optimizer steps usually help val_bpb.

title: Cosine-shaped warmdown
spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape: multiplier = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1-FINAL_LR_FRAC)*0.5*(1+cos(pi*(1-frac_remaining)))over the warmdown portion.

title: Depth 6 wider-per-time
spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim 384 via ASPECT_RATIO 64); a smaller model gets more steps in 300 s. Optionally pair with ASPECT_RATIO 96 to keep width.

title: Short warmup 0.03
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to smooth early training, especially with Muon at LR 0.04.

title: Gradient clipping at 1.0
spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before optimizer step, to stabilize with the high LR.

title: Lower total batch to 2**17
spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 (grad accumulation of 1 when seq len 2048). Many more steps; consider scaling MATRIX_LR down slightly (0.03) if unstable.

title: Adam beta2 0.98
spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.98) for smoother second-moment estimates.

title: Head dim 64
spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 to double the number of attention heads (adjust KV heads consistently if the code ties them to n_head).

title: Squared ReLU to ReLU-GLU variant
spec: Replace the MLP activation relu(x)^2 with SwiGLU, using hidden size 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64 to keep parameter count equal.

title: Warmdown ratio 0.7
spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 so the LR decays linearly over a longer fraction of the time budget.

title: Deep Supervision with Intermediate Loss
spec: Add a secondary loss term that compares the output of the last 2 residual blocks directly to the target, scaled to 10% of the main loss. This encourages deeper layer convergence earlier.

title: Muon NS steps 4
spec: Reduce Muon Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 4 to cut optimizer overhead and gain steps.

title: Warmdown ratio 0.3
spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 to keep high LR longer before decaying.

title: Learn Rate Rampdown Schedule
spec: Replace the linear warmdown schedule with a cosine-shaped decay starting at WARMDOWN_RATIO. Add the import for torch.cos Perspektiven and insert the calculations at the top of the loss function before optimizer step.

title: Layer-wise Weight Decay Magnitude Scaling
spec: Modify the weight decay loop to apply 0.1 decay to input and recurrent weights, but 0.001 decay to the large output projection weights. This balances regularization between early recurrent dynamics and final output calibration.

title: Aspect ratio 80
spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO = 80 at DEPTH 8 for a wider model (dim 640, ensuring it is a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128).

title: Unembedding LR Increase
spec: Increase the learning rate for the lm_head (unembedding) layer to <NEW_UNEMBEDDING_LR>. This should help the model converge faster at the output layer.

title: Muon momentum warmup shorter/higher
spec: Change Muon momentum schedule to ramp 0.85→0.95 over the first 100 steps, then hold 0.95 until warmdown, and drop to 0.90 in the final part of warmdown.

title: Weight decay 0.1
spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1 for cautious Muon weight decay, since training is short.

title: LinearWarmingUp
spec: Change WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.05 to introduce a warmup phase, which often stabilizes training dynamics and improves generalization.

title: CosSchedule
spec: Replace linear schedule with cosine based schedule initialization and final learning rate decay for LR

title: WarmupSchedule
spec: Use a warmup schedule with a cosine decay

title: DirectLRAnnealing
spec: Replace the using avariable beta values for Adam, e.g. using ADAM_BETAS (0.9, 0.95) instead of (0.8, 0.95).

title: MultiDLr
spec: Use different learning rates for different parameter types, e.g. 0.001 for weights and 0.0001 for biases

title: Smaller model, more tokens (DEPTH 6, AR 64)

title: Final LR fraction 0.05
spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.05 so that the LR does not drop all the way to zero at the end of warmdown. Change only this constant.

title: Raise UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.008
spec: Slot 4 showed that raising the lm_head LR helped (1.1108). Push further: set UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.008 (if slot 4 used a different value, double that value). This tests whether the gain continues and whether it is real.

title: SoftWarmingUp
spec: Add a softwarmpending phase, which might help early training stability.

title: CosineDecay

spec: Change TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 so grad accumulation drops from 8 to 4 steps... adjust accordingly so that the assertion on divisibility holds). In a fixed 300 s budget, more optimizer steps on a small model usually helps. Leave learning rates unchanged.

The goal is higher throughput, so more tokens are seen in 300 s. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Shorter warmdown, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.3

title: Lower Muon weight decay with linear decay to zero
spec: Replace constant WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 by a schedule where weight decay is multiplied by the current LR multiplier (progress-based) so decay fades to 0 during warmdown. If it is already multiplied by the LR multiplier, instead set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1. Change only the weight decay term.

title: Raise Muon matrix LR to 0.05
spec: Change MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05, and keep everything else fixed. Muon LR is often under-tuned for short runs.

title: Bolder: depth 4, wider
spec: Set DEPTH to 4 and ASPECT_RATIO to 128 so model_dim is 512 (4 heads at HEAD_DIM 128). A shallower but wider model is faster per step and sees more tokens in 300 s. Keep other hyperparameters. Check VRAM stays fine.

title: Weight decay 0.1

title: Unembedding LR 0.008

title: Short warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to soften early instability with Muon and Adam at high LRs.

title: Gradient clipping at 1.0
spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before the optimizer step, after the accumulation loop. This helps stability at high LRs.

title: Untied value-embedding drop

title: Depth 6 wider-per-time

title: Wider Depth (6 layers, 64:16 dim)
spec: Set DEPTH = 6, ASPECT_RATIO = 64, HEAD_DIM = 64 to achieve a 1024-dim model (9048 trained tokens at 256 K) at a similar cost to the incumbent, testing if a marginally larger initial model capacity beats the smaller, noise-y incumbent.

title: Linear Decay Warmup Schedule
spec: Replace WARMUP_RATIO=0.0 with WARMUP_RATIO=0.05 and add an exponential decay schedule using WARMUP_RATIO * (1 - time/time_budget) that gradually reduces the learning rate over the training lifetime, avoiding sharp drops.

title: Hard Negative Prompting
spec: Randomly flip output logits with low probability to introduce controlled difficulty in the training signal without altering ground truth.

title: Burst-Size Learning Rate
spec: Apply bursts of learning rate changes at the start of each epoch to improve convergence.

title: Adaptive Warmup Ratio
spec: Increase initial warmup and decay faster once a running validation loss plateau is detected.

title: Temporal Frequency Loss
spec: Regulate the temporal frequency of output patterns using a loss term on time-varying output variances.

title: Attention Span Heuristic
spec: Modulate effective attention spans by varying the weight of self-attention masks over time.

title: Oracle Loss Conditioning
spec: Supervise the loss function with oracle conditions that penalize over-constrained sequences.

title: Curriculum Learning by Attention Span
spec: Gradually increase the sliding window ATTN context size during training to encourage model robustness via incremental complexity.

title: Depth-Aware Attention Masking
spec: Apply a depth-dependent masking strategy in transformer blocks to refine attention balance, improving generalization.

title: Embedding Layerwise LR
spec: Apply a per-layer learning rate multiplier to the embedding matrix to reduce asymmetry in parameter updates.

title: Embedding and LM Head Uncertainty
spec: Constrain the LM Head and token embeddings to have a maximum norm or variance penalty, preventing them from dominating the loss and forcing deeper layers to drive the gradient signal during training.

title: Layerwise Gradient Norm Scaling
spec: Apply a dynamic multiplier to gradients of each layer based on the target layer's depth (e.g., deeper layers scaled down to match shallow layers' variance) to ensure uniform gradient magnitudes across the network, helping convergence.

title: Depth 10 model

spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to soften early instability, especially with Muon and the high embedding LR.

title: Aspect ratio 80 at depth 8
spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO = 80 (dim 640) keeping DEPTH 8, for a wider model; HEAD_DIM 128 gives 5 heads.

title: ReLU^2 to SwiGLU-ish smaller MLP
spec: Replace the MLP activation relu(x)^2 with a gated variant (SwiGLU with hidden = 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64) keeping the parameter count about equal.

title: Longer warmdown ratio 0.7
spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 to test whether more annealing helps in the short budget.

title: Apply layer-wise learning rate scaling (MuG)
spec: Combine the Muon optimizer with linearly interpolated learning rates per layer using the MoG variant, instead of a single global per-layer scale. This tailors updates more finely by layer.

title: Depth 6 wider-per-step
spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim = 384 with ASPECT_RATIO 64; consider ASPECT_RATIO 96 to keep dim ~576, and HEAD_DIM 128 divides it). Smaller model processes more tokens in 300 s.

title: Unembedding LR 0.008
spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008.

spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05 for faster Muon progress in the short run.

spec: For the first 25% of the time budget, train on the first 512 tokens of each sequence (slice inputs and targets to [:, :512]) to get more steps per second. After that use the full sequence length. Mark the model for dynamic=False recompile only once, and accept one recompile at the switch point, which is not counted in training time. Keep the loss normalisation per token.

title: Gradient clipping at 1.0
spec: After the backward pass, and before optimizer.step(), call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0). Do this once per optimizer step, after all micro-batches are accumulated. Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Cosine-shaped warmdown
spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape: with progress p in the warmdown phase, use lr_mult = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1-FINAL_LR_FRAC)*0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)).

title: Final LR fraction 0.05
spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not fully reach zero at the end of the warmdown.

title: Warmdown ratio 0.7
spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the LR decays linearly over more of the time budget.

title: Depth 6 wider-per-time
spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim = 384 with ASPECT_RATIO 64). A smaller model gets more steps in 300 s. Then try ASPECT_RATIO 96 if the code permits, to keep the width up.

title: Depth 10
spec: Set DEPTH = 10, keeping ASPECT_RATIO at 64, and lower DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 if it OOMs. Check whether the larger model pays off despite fewer steps.

title: Disable torch compile mode tweaks: max-autotune
spec: If torch.compile is used on the model, try mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs'. Compile time is not counted, and faster kernels give more steps in 300 s.

title: Head dim 64
spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 to get more attention heads. This is cheap to test.

title: Muon momentum warmup shorter/higher
spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule so it ramps to 0.97 within 100 steps rather than the current ramp. If the schedule is already like this, raise the final momentum from 0.95 to 0.97.

title: Squared-ReLU to SwiGLU-free tweak: MLP ratio 3
spec: Reduce the MLP hidden expansion from 4x to 3x. That frees compute for more steps. Alternatively keep 4x and test it against this.

title: Muon LR 0.06 plus Newton-Schulz 4 steps
spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 and reduce the Muon Newton-Schulz iteration count from 5 to 4 to save per-step time. This is a single bolder optimizer change targeting a faster per-step rate in the small model.

title: All-short windows except last
spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSS". The code should still force the final layer to full attention. This tests the speed gain from cheaper attention.

title: Weight EMA for evaluation
spec: Keep an exponential moving average of model weights (decay 0.999 per step, updated every step with torch._foreach_lerp_ on a copy of the parameters in bf16/fp32). Swap the EMA weights in just before the final evaluation call, without touching the evaluation code itself, by copying the EMA into the model params after the training loop ends. Only do this if it does not touch the eval call or the summary printing.

title: Depth 4 with wider dim (ASPECT_RATIO 128)
spec: Set DEPTH=4 and ASPECT_RATIO=128 so model_dim is 512 (a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128, giving 4 heads). The shallower model has cheaper, faster steps and sees more tokens within 300 s. Change nothing else.

title: Time-based LR warmup 5% plus warmdown 0.4
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO=0.05 and WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.4 and keep FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.05. Combine the small positive signals into one run. Check that the schedule function handles warmup as a fraction of the elapsed time progress.

title: Warmdown ratio 0.3
spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3, giving more time at full LR.

title: Lower logit softcap to 15
spec: Change the logit softcap constant (currently probably 15 or 30 in the forward pass, where logits = softcap * tanh(logits/softcap)) to 10 if it's 15+, or leave the form unchanged and just reduce the constant. Tests the stabilizing effect on a short run.

title: Short warmup plus Muon LR 0.05
spec: Set MATRIX_LR = 0.05 and WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 together. The warmup stabilizes the larger LR; both earlier small gains pointed toward a slightly higher LR on the depth-6 model.

title: Matrix LR 0.05
spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05.

title: Zero init of projection and value-embedding gate tweaks
spec: Make sure the output projections of attention and MLP are zero-initialized. If they already are, change the residual-lambda init from 1.0 to 0.9 for the x0 skip scalars.

title: Weight decay 0.1
spec: Lower the Muon cautious WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1. The short run may need less regularization.

title: Gradient clipping 1.0
spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before the optimizer step. This stabilizes the Adam-trained embeddings at the high LR of 0.6.

title: Short warmup
spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to stabilize the first steps of Muon and Adam at high LRs.

title: Scalar LR 0.25
spec: Halve SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 for the per-layer scalar parameters.

title: Depth 6, wider-per-compute
spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim = 384 with ASPECT_RATIO 64). A smaller model gets more tokens in 300 s. Check that the dim is a multiple of HEAD_DIM. If it isn't, set ASPECT_RATIO = 86 so the dim becomes 516, then round to 512.

title: Head dim 64
spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 to double the number of attention heads. This may improve quality at similar cost on the A100 with flash attention.

title: Matrix LR 0.03
spec: Lower MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.03 to check whether the current value is too high.

title: Warmdown ratio 0.35
spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.35 to leave more time at peak LR.

title: Muon momentum warmup shorter
spec: Shorten the Muon momentum ramp from 0.85 to 0.95. Make it reach 0.95 within the first 100 steps instead of 300. Or, if the ramp is time-based, make it reach 0.95 at 10% of the budget.

title: Disable gradient-free overhead: eval-less loop
spec: Remove any periodic logging that calls .item() or cuda synchronize on every step. Sync only every 50 steps. This removes host stalls and gives more steps in the fixed time budget. Keep the time accounting intact.

title: Total batch 2**18 with device batch 64
spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 so each optimizer step uses 4 micro-batches of 64x2048 instead of 8 (grad accumulation halves). With only 300 s of training the smaller model benefits from more optimizer steps. Leave LRs unchanged. If Muon momentum warmup is step-based it will scale naturally.

title: Embedding LR 0.4
spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4. This tests the Adam LR for token embeddings.

title: Warmdown ratio 0.65
spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.65 so the LR decays linearly over a longer final portion of the time budget.

title: Ramp sequence-free: Adam beta1 0.9 and beta2 0.99 with clipping 1.0
spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.9, 0.99) and add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) right before the optimizer step, after the last micro-batch backward. Combines two earlier small gains with smoother Adam statistics for embeddings and scalars.

title: Depth 5 with wider model
spec: Set DEPTH = 5 and ASPECT_RATIO = 77 so model_dim is about 385; if required, round so model_dim is a multiple of HEAD_DIM (128), e.g. ASPECT_RATIO = 76.8 -> use dim 384. Keep all else unchanged. Tests whether fewer, wider layers give more steps in the fixed 300 s and better bpb. Make sure the window pattern string still works for 5 layers (last layer is always full).

title: All-long windows (WINDOW_PATTERN L)
spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "L" so every layer uses full-context attention. With a shrunken 6-layer model the sliding window may hurt more than it saves; flash attention full causal is fast enough on A100. Only change the constant.

title: Adam beta2 0.99
spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.8, 0.99) for smoother second-moment estimates on the embeddings and scalars.

title: SwiGLU-style gated MLP with matched params
spec: Replace the ReLU^2 MLP with a gated MLP: out = c_proj(silu(c_fc_gate(x)) * c_fc_up(x)), with hidden dim = round(8/3 * n_embd) to a multiple of 64 so parameter count stays about equal. Keep c_proj zero-initialized and all matrices in the Muon group.

title: Cosine decay for Muon learning rate
spec: Replace the linear-to-zero decay for the Muon learning rate (lr_factor2 = 1 - step/total) with a cosine decay, lr_factor2 = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*step/total)). Keep the bias and head SGD schedules linear. Also keep the Muon target magnitude schedule inside _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 as it is. The cosine shape keeps more learning rate in the middle of training and drops it faster at the end.

title: Four-view test-time augmentation
spec: In infer's tta path, extend the views for the uncertain subset from two shifted crops plus the original to four shifted corner crops (pad=1, adding the crop_tr and crop_bl windows from the reflect-padded input), with flips, so the average is over 8 views. The change is inside _get_tta_logits and only affects the 25 percent least-confident images. It may recover a little accuracy at a small prediction-time cost.

title: Five Newton-Schulz iterations
spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, increase the number of Newton-Schulz iterations from 3 to 5 by repeating the A/B/X update block two more times. Accuracy of the orthogonalisation improves, at the cost of extra batched matmuls on tiny (≤256x256 padded) matrices. Because the step is compiled, check it adds little wall time; if the gain is negligible the variant is not worth keeping.

title: Residual connection in ConvGroup
spec: Add an identity shortcut around conv2 within ConvGroup for blocks where channels_in equals channels_out (block2 and block3 do not match block1's 64 to 256 input, so only use it for block3's 256 to 256 path). Implement as x = x + conv2_output before norm2 (or after norm2, keeping the BatchNorm without scale). The shortcut lets gradients flow through the deeper block at negligible extra compute.

title: Warm-up for Muon learning rate
spec: Add a short linear warm-up to the Muon learning rate: over the first 3% of total_train_steps, multiply the Muon lr factor by step/warm_steps, then apply the existing linear decay for the rest. Implement inside the per-step lr computation in train() (lr_factor2 = min(1, step/warm_steps) * (1 - step*lr_factor2_base)). This protects the first Newton-Schulz-orthogonalised updates, which are the largest relative steps early on.

title: Larger translation with reflect pad
spec: Increase TRANSLATE from 2 to 3 so that the random crop offset ranges over 7 positions per axis instead of 5, with the reflect padding automatically sized by the existing pad logic. Also change the test-time pad in infer's _get_tta_logits from 1 to match a 2-pixel shift set only if accuracy holds. This is a one-constant change to the augmentation strength; it mainly tests whether the small 60-epoch-equivalent budget is under- or over-regularised by translation.

title: Progressive resolution from 24 to 32 pixels
spec: During the first ~40% of training steps, downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 with bilinear interpolation (antialias on), and switch to the native 32x32 for the rest. The whitening conv and max-pool stack are size-agnostic, so the head still sees a 1x1 map after the final MaxPool2d(3) only at 32; to keep it consistent, use adaptive average pooling to 1x1 in the head path only if the spatial size is not 32. Compile both shapes once in the untimed warm-up if possible, or accept one recompile. This aims to cut time per early step substantially at similar final accuracy.

title: Replace GELU at input with identity
spec: Remove the leading nn.GELU() applied to the whitening output in self.layers (the whitening layer has a bias, and the first ConvGroup's conv1 is linear anyway). This drops one elementwise kernel per forward and backward pass. Verify the whitened features keep their sign information; if accuracy drops, revert.

title: Label smoothing ramp
spec: Make LABEL_SMOOTHING time-dependent: start at 0.0 at the first step and rise linearly to 0.09 by the middle of training, then hold. The loss is computed inside forward_step, so pass the current smoothing value as a tensor argument to the compiled function to avoid recompilation (or pre-compute a small table). Early training then fits hard targets, while later epochs get the regularisation.

title: Per-sample random horizontal flip
spec: Replace the alternating-epoch whole-dataset flip with an independent random flip per sample in every epoch. In the loader, the pre-flipped copy is no longer needed; apply batch_flip_lr to the normalised images at the start of each epoch (it is already compiled). Keep the random 2-pixel translation and color jitter unchanged. This trades the current flip diversity scheme for per-sample flips and may change the optimum epoch count slightly, so leave EPOCHS unchanged.

title: Squared-ReLU in place of SiLU
spec: Replace the nn.SiLU activation in ConvGroup (both uses) with a squared ReLU, defined as relu(x) squared, implemented as a small nn.Module whose forward returns F.relu(x).square(). Leave the input GELU and every other part of the network unchanged. Because squared ReLU has a different scale than SiLU, the following batch norm (which has no learned scale unless changed) absorbs the scale; keep the rest of the schedule as is. Expect a different time and accuracy trade-off, so check both.

title: Switch off horizontal flip for the final 20 percent of steps
spec: In the loader, keep the existing alternating-epoch flip for the first 80 percent of total_train_steps, then stop flipping entirely for the last 20 percent so the final fits see only the native orientation that the test set uses. Implement this by checking the global step against 0.8*total_train_steps inside train(), and passing a flag that suppresses the epoch-parity flip in __iter__. Brightness, contrast and translation stay on throughout.

title: Concatenated max and mean pooling before the head
spec: Replace nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) in CifarNet.layers with a module that returns the concatenation of the spatial max and the spatial mean along the channel axis, giving 512 features for block3 width 256. Change the head to nn.Linear(512, 10, bias=False) and keep the division by x.size(-1) in forward, using the new feature count in place of the old one so the output scale is comparable. Mean pooling gives the head a smoother global signal alongside the peak response. Keep everything else unchanged, including the head LR and weight decay.

title: Stop colour jitter for the final 20 percent of steps
spec: In train(), disable the brightness and contrast jitter once step reaches 0.8 * total_train_steps, so the last fifth of training sees clean normalised images. Implement this by making CifarLoader.__iter__ take the current step or a flag, or by setting the color_jitter enabled flag on the loader when the threshold is crossed; the loader's epoch-level augmentation is applied once per epoch, so apply the switch at the start of the epoch that contains the threshold. Keep flip and translation unchanged. This is a data-side annealing that removes a source of train-test mismatch near the end of training.

title: Nesterov off for Muon
spec: Set nesterov=False for the Muon optimizer in train() (it is currently True) so that the orthogonalised update uses the plain momentum buffer. This is a single-flag change to test whether the Nesterov look-ahead is useful at this learning rate. It removes one foreach add per step.

title: Muon momentum warm-up
spec: Ramp the Muon momentum from 0.85 at step 0 to MUON_MOMENTUM (0.655) at about 10% of total steps, in the optimizer's step (update group['momentum'] each step, which Muon reads from the param group). Momentum for the early steps is then higher for smoother directions, and the final value matches the tuned constant. Keep the Nesterov form unchanged.

title: Longer whitening-bias training
spec: Increase WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS from 0.2 to 1.0 so the whitening-layer bias keeps training for the first full epoch. Currently the bias only trains for a short initial window and then freezes via whiten_bias_grad. Keep BIAS_LR and the linear decay for that group as they are. This is a one-constant change to test whether the learned input offset helps.

title: Confidence-free TTA on all images
spec: Remove the confidence-based selection in predict and apply the full flip and shift ensemble (the _get_tta_logits path) to every test image, dropping the topk step. This simplifies the prediction function and makes its cost deterministic. Compare accuracy and prediction time against the current 25 percent selection; the expected gain is small but the code becomes simpler.

title: Wider prediction TTA: five shifts with flips
spec: In infer()'s tta path, add two more shifted views (offsets (0,2) and (2,0) in addition to the current top-left and bottom-right crops, from a reflect-pad of 1 pixel) so each uncertain image is averaged over more views before flipping. Keep the 25 percent uncertainty selection. Tests whether extra test-time views buy accuracy cheaply, since predict time is small relative to training.

title: Residual skip inside the second conv of each group
spec: In ConvGroup.forward, after conv2 and norm2 but before the final activation, add the input to the group's pooled output x_pool (the tensor after pool, before norm1) when the channel counts match. Only block2 and block3 match shapes with their conv2 output if the channel counts are equal, so apply the skip only when channels_in == channels_out (block3 input is 256, output 256). Adds almost no compute. Tests whether a residual path helps the deeper block.

title: Batch size 2048 with scaled learning rates
spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 2048 and scale BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(2048/1536) (about 1.15) so the per-step update magnitude stays comparable. The number of steps drops by about a quarter at the same EPOCHS, which lowers time per epoch through better GPU utilisation. Weight decay is already scaled by batch size inside train(). Tests the speed-accuracy tradeoff on the batch axis.

title: Brightness and contrast jitter off
spec: Set the color_jitter enabled flag to False in train()'s aug dict so only flip and translate remain. Removes the batch_color_jitter op from each epoch. The jitter magnitudes were tuned but its removal is a clean ablation that measures how much regularization the photometric augmentation contributes at 7.65 epochs.

title: Lighter middle block width
spec: Change widths in CifarNet from block1=64, block2=256, block3=256 to block1=64, block2=192, block3=256 (or the equivalent reduction in block2 only). The second block dominates FLOPs at 16x16 resolution, so reducing it cuts time roughly in proportion. Keep the head input size consistent with block3. Tests the time-accuracy frontier along the width axis.

title: Use Muon for the head as well
spec: The head weight is a 2D matrix of shape (10,256) and currently uses Nesterov SGD. Move model.head.weight into the Muon parameter group by handling 2D params in the Muon path: pass it to Muon separately and reshape within the existing 4D-only filter list by adding a branch that treats 2D tensors as (D,K) with no reshape. Keep the head LR at HEAD_LR scale multiplied by the existing factor. Tests whether orthogonalised updates help the classifier layer.

title: Larger translation pad with reflect padding
spec: Set TRANSLATE to 4 (pad 4 with reflect, random crop back to 32x32) so each image can shift up to 4 pixels; the crop helper already supports any r because it computes r=(H_padded-crop_size)//2. Predict-time TTA in infer() currently hard-codes pad=1 and crops at 0:32 and 2:34; leave that as is. Tests stronger translation augmentation.

title: Recalibrate BatchNorm statistics after training
spec: At the end of train(), before returning, recompute BatchNorm running statistics on clean data. Set each BatchNorm module's momentum to None (cumulative average), reset its running stats with reset_running_stats(), and run the model in train mode under torch.no_grad() on the un-augmented, un-flipped normalized training images in batches of 2000, using the same forward path as training. Then restore momentum to 1 - 0.5566 and switch back to eval. The statistics then match the unaugmented test distribution rather than the running averages collected under flip, shift and jitter. Do not change predict(), which must not modify the model. This runs only inside train() and uses images from the current run, so the reuse rule holds.

title: Nonzero LR floor at the end of training
spec: Change the linear decay of all learning-rate multipliers so they decay to 0.1 of their initial value instead of 0. In train(), replace lr_factor1 = 1 - step * lr_factor1_base with lr_factor1 = 1 - 0.9 * step * lr_factor1_base, and similarly for lr_factor2 = 1 - 0.9 * step * lr_factor2_base. Keep the same base step counts. The floor keeps the final updates from vanishing, which may help the averaged test predictions. This is a one-line change to each factor, plus the matching change in the Muon target-magnitude end value if needed (leave it unchanged for the first run).

title: Probability averaging in test-time augmentation
spec: In infer(), inside the tta function and the _get_tta_logits helper, change the aggregation so that the softmax of each view is averaged instead of the raw logits. Specifically, in _get_tta_logits replace averaged_logits = reshaped_logits.mean(dim=0) with averaged_logits = torch.log(reshaped_logits.softmax(dim=-1).mean(dim=0) + 1e-12). Keep the view construction unchanged. The argmax of the output is then the argmax of the mean probability. The log keeps the output as logits of the expected form. Do not change the uncertainty selection, which still uses initial_logits. This is a small change to the prediction function only.

title: Per-channel brightness and contrast jitter
spec: Change the color jitter so that brightness and contrast are drawn independently for each colour channel rather than once per image. In batch_color_jitter, sample a brightness shift and a contrast scale of shape (B, 3, 1, 1) instead of (B, 1, 1, 1), with the same ranges as now. Apply them as before. This adds colour-balance variation that the global jitter does not produce. The compute cost is unchanged. Keep the same enable flag and ranges so the comparison isolates this change.

title: Learnable head output scale
spec: The head currently returns self.head(x) / x.size(-1), a fixed scale. Replace that constant with a learnable scalar parameter, initialised to 1/x.size(-1) and trained with the head's Nesterov SGD group and no weight decay. The head weight is still re-normalised in reset(). This lets the network learn its own logit temperature, which interacts with label smoothing. Keep the parameter in fp32 or half as the rest of the head is, and make sure it is reset in reset() so every run starts from the same init.

title: Muon gradient-norm rescale every step
spec: In Muon.step, the gradient-norm rescaling is applied only every norm_freq steps, and norm_freq grows from 2 to 17 over training. Set the rescaling to run on every step (norm_freq fixed at 1) and keep the rest of the update as is. This removes the staleness of the cached scale factors late in training, when the gradient norms change quickly. The compute cost is one extra foreach norm per step, which is small next to Newton-Schulz.

title: Random per-sample horizontal flip instead of alternating epochs
spec: Replace the epoch-alternating flip in CifarLoader.__iter__ with an independent per-sample flip each epoch: call batch_flip_lr on the whole augmented batch inside the loop before yielding, and drop the epoch%2 flip branch. Keep the pre-flipped cache removed accordingly. Tests whether per-sample randomness beats the every-other-epoch scheme at this short schedule.

title: Progressive resolution during training
spec: In train(), for the first ~40% of steps downsample each augmented batch to 24x24 with F.interpolate(mode='bilinear', antialias=True), then use full 32x32 for the rest. The network is fully convolutional up to the final MaxPool2d(3) which assumes a 3x3 map, so instead keep the spatial path at 32 by only using the downscaled batch for the first phase with an added adaptive pool so the head still sees 256 features. Keep the compiled forward_step with dynamic=False by compiling a second graph for the low-res shape. Goal: fewer FLOPs early on for the same epoch count.

title: Drop the whitening bias update after the first phase by freezing it
spec: Remove the whiten bias from the optimizer entirely (do not add it to param_configs) and always pass whiten_bias_grad=False into the model, so the whitening bias stays at its initialised value of zero. This removes one parameter group and the branch in forward. Tests whether the 0.2-epoch whiten bias training contributes measurable accuracy.

title: Five-view TTA with diagonal shifts
spec: In _get_tta_logits, extend the views beyond the current original plus two corner crops of the reflect-padded image. Add the two remaining diagonal 2-pixel crops (top-right and bottom-left) so there are five shifted views, each also flipped. Average all logits equally. Keep the rest of the pipeline and predict() unchanged.

title: Label smoothing schedule
spec: Replace the fixed LABEL_SMOOTHING of 0.09 with a schedule that starts at 0.2 and linearly decays to 0.0 over total_train_steps. Set the value in forward_step through a mutable tensor or a Python float recomputed each step. Label smoothing is a regulariser that matters less near the end of short training.

title: Muon momentum warmup
spec: Ramp MUON_MOMENTUM linearly from 0.5 at step 0 up to the configured 0.655 over the first 10 percent of total_train_steps. Update group['momentum'] in optimizer2 each step inside train(), before opt.step(). Early steps then take smaller, less noisy orthogonalised updates while the momentum buffer is still filling.

title: Trapezoidal LR schedule
spec: Keep the LR constant at its initial value for the first 60 percent of total_train_steps, then decay linearly to zero over the last 40 percent. Use this in place of the current linear-from-start decay, for both lr_factor1 and lr_factor2. The high-LR plateau may improve accuracy at the same step count.

title: Dropout before the head
spec: Add nn.Dropout(0.1) on the flattened features before self.head in CifarNet.forward. It is active only in model.train() mode, so predict() is unaffected. This is a light regulariser and may help a little at 7.65 epochs.

title: Learnable head output scale
spec: Replace the fixed division by x.size(-1) in CifarNet.forward with a learnable scalar parameter initialised to 1/x.size(-1) (for example a 1-element nn.Parameter). Include it in the SGD group with the head, so the logit scale can adapt during training. Keep reset() consistent with the new parameter.

title: Test-time BN recalibration on a copy
spec: In predict(), deep-copy the model, recompute the BatchNorm running statistics on the test images in train-mode forward passes with momentum None (cumulative average) on the copy, then run infer on the copy. The original model is never modified, which satisfies the rule against changing it in predict. This tests whether test-set statistics help.

title: Residual skip around conv2 in each ConvGroup
spec: In ConvGroup.forward, add a skip connection around the second convolution: after norm1 and the first SiLU, save x as identity, then compute conv2 -> norm2 -> SiLU and return that output plus identity. The first ConvGroup has 64 channels in and 64 out after conv1, but block2 and block3 change width (64->256, 256->256), so apply the skip only when channel counts match, or use a 1x1 conv without bias for the mismatched block. Keep the BatchNorm without learned scale, and keep the Muon/SGD grouping unchanged.

title: Progressive resolution: train early epochs at 28x28
spec: For the first 40 percent of training steps, downsample each augmented training batch from 32x32 to 28x28 with F.interpolate (bilinear, antialias=True), so early steps are cheaper. Switch to full 32x32 for the remaining steps. Keep the whitening init on full-resolution images, and keep the model unchanged: at 28x28 the spatial sizes go 27, 13, 6, 3 and the final MaxPool2d(3) still reduces to 1x1. Predict and the TTA path stay at 32x32. Everything else (LR schedules, augmentation order, batch size) stays the same.

title: Remove color jitter augmentation
spec: Set the color_jitter entry in the train() aug dict to enabled False, so batch_color_jitter is never called. This removes one compiled augmentation pass per epoch. The 7.65 epoch budget stays fixed, so accuracy may drop slightly but runtime also drops slightly.

title: Remove the initial GELU before the first ConvGroup
spec: In CifarNet, delete the nn.GELU() at the start of self.layers so the whitening convolution feeds straight into the first ConvGroup. This removes one nonlinearity on the whitened features and saves a small elementwise kernel. Nothing else changes: the whitening weights stay frozen, and the whiten bias keeps its warmup schedule.

title: Cosine LR decay
spec: Replace the linear-to-zero decay for both optimizers with cosine decay to zero: factor = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*step/total_train_steps)). Apply it to lr_factor1 for the bias group and lr_factor2 for the Muon and head groups in train(). Muon's target magnitude decay in _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 can stay linear.

title: Translation of 3 pixels
spec: Change TRANSLATE from 2 to 3. The reflect padding in CifarLoader and the batch_crop helper already take the pad from the config, so only the constant needs changing. Also update the TTA pad in infer() from 1 to 2 so the test-time shifts match. This tests stronger translation augmentation.

title: Cutout regularisation
spec: Add cutout to the augmentation: for each training batch, with probability 0.5 per image, zero out a random 8x8 square of the normalised images (set to 0 after normalisation, which is the mean colour). Implement it inside a small torch.compile'd helper applied in CifarLoader.__iter__ after translation. Keep all other augmentation as is.

title: Three-stage resolution ramp
spec: Extend the progressive resolution from slot 9. For the first 40 percent of steps use 24x24 bilinear resizing, for the next 30 percent use 28x28, and for the final 30 percent use the full 32x32 images with no resize. Keep antialias=True. Pick the stage from step relative to total_train_steps inside the training loop, with no other change to the schedule, augmentation or model.

title: Polar Express Newton-Schulz coefficients
spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, replace the single fixed (a, b, c) = (3.4576, -4.7391, 2.0843) with a different triple for each of the three iterations, taken from the Polar Express minimax sequence (for example (8.2051, -22.9019, 16.4607), (4.0415, -2.9472, 0.5424), (3.8916, -2.8148, 0.5151)). Keep the target-magnitude scaling and the transpose logic unchanged. Use the three triples in order inside the unrolled loop. No other hyperparameter changes.

title: AdamW for head and norm biases
spec: Replace the Nesterov SGD optimizer1 with AdamW for the parameter groups holding the whiten bias, the norm biases and the linear head. Use betas (0.9, 0.99), eps 1e-8, and base lrs of about 1e-3 for the bias group and 2e-3 for the head, scaled by the same linear-to-zero decay that already multiplies each group. Set weight decay to WEIGHT_DECAY * BATCH_SIZE / lr to match the current decoupled decay. Keep the Muon optimizer for conv filters unchanged.

title: Anti-aliased blur pooling
spec: Replace each nn.MaxPool2d(2) in ConvGroup with a blur-pool: a fixed 3x3 binomial low-pass filter ([1,2,1]/4 outer product, depthwise via groups=channels, stride 1 with reflect padding), followed by a stride-2 subsample, and keep max pooling after the blur. Create the filter as a buffer with the model's half dtype and channels_last layout. Leave the final MaxPool2d(3) unchanged.

title: Extra shifted views in TTA
spec: Add two more shifted views to the TTA views in _get_tta_logits, for example the (0,2) and (2,0) corners from the reflect-padded images, so that the averaged logits use five translations and their flips. The output stays a mean over views. Compile shape stays fixed because the number of views is constant.

title: Progressive resolution with downscaled early epochs
spec: For the first ~30% of epochs, downscale the training images to 24x24 with area interpolation (F.interpolate, cheap) before the pad and crop step, then switch to 32x32 for the remaining epochs. Compiled forward_step will recompile once for the new shape, which happens during the untimed warm-up only if shapes are fixed, so keep the two shapes fixed across runs. Predict stays at 32x32.

title: Muon Newton-Schulz on each channel group in a single batched call
spec: Group the filter tensors by identical reshaped (D, K) shape before padding, so that the Newton-Schulz batch is split into a few uniform stacks instead of one padded stack. This reduces wasted FLOPs on padding when block1 (K=27 or 24) and block2/3 (K=2304) are padded to the same max_K. Only the internal stacking code of Muon changes.

title: Label smoothing annealed to zero
spec: Make LABEL_SMOOTHING a per-step value that decays linearly from its current 0.09 to 0 over the training steps, using the existing step counter. Inside forward_step, pass the current smoothing as a Python float argument, or keep it as a 0-dim tensor to avoid recompilation. Predict and the rest of the loop are unchanged.

title: Batch size ramp
spec: Start training with batch size 768 and grow it to 1536 in two or three steps across training, keeping the per-step learning rates scaled by the batch ratio so the effective step size is similar. Each batch size needs a fixed shape to avoid repeated compilation, so restrict the steps to two or three sizes. Update the loader's batch size and the step count accordingly.

title: Short linear warmup for Muon learning rate
spec: Multiply the Muon group lr by a linear warmup factor min(1, (step+1)/W) with W about 3% of total_train_steps, combined with the existing linear-to-zero decay. Apply it in the same place where lr_factor2 is set in the training loop, leaving the SGD groups unchanged.

title: Mixed per-batch brightness and contrast jitter with a cap
spec: Reduce the color jitter to brightness only, or contrast only, on alternate epochs, or apply jitter to half of each batch. This tests whether the current combined jitter at 0.14 and 0.13 is more than the short schedule needs. The change is in the aug dictionary and the batch_color_jitter call, not the optimiser.

title: Larger batch during the low-resolution phase
spec: Use a bigger batch while the input is downscaled, for example 3072 for the first 30% of steps, then 1536 for the rest. Each stage's Muon and SGD learning rates are scaled by sqrt(new_batch/1536) at that stage, and weight decay is scaled with the batch as the script already does. Split the loader into stages, or re-batch the same permutation with a stage-dependent batch size. Keep len(train_loader)-based step counting consistent by computing total_train_steps from the sample count, so the total epoch budget is unchanged.

title: Nesterov off for Muon
spec: Set nesterov=False for the Muon optimizer (the second optimizer) and keep the other settings. This drops the extra foreach_add for the nesterov buffer. Test whether accuracy holds at the same epoch count, since the momentum schedule was tuned with Nesterov on.

title: Nesterov off for the SGD bias and head optimizer
spec: Set nesterov=False in the torch.optim.SGD call that creates optimizer1, so the bias, norm-bias, and head updates use plain momentum. Keep SGD_MOMENTUM and the learning-rate schedule unchanged. The Muon optimizer keeps its own Nesterov setting. This is a one-line change that tests whether the classical momentum form is better for the small-scale parameters at this short schedule.

title: Three-stage progressive resolution (16, 24, 32)
spec: Extend the existing low-res schedule into three stages. For the first 15% of total_train_steps, downscale each batch with F.interpolate(size=(16,16), mode='area'). From 15% to 45%, use size (24,24). After that, use the native 32x32. Keep the rest of train() unchanged, including the whiten-init on full-resolution images and the forward_step compile. Compute the stage boundaries from total_train_steps, and keep the forward_step compile as is, accepting a recompile per shape. If recompiles are costly, mark the stage input shapes as dynamic=False or pre-warm them in the untimed call.

title: Whitening layer with kernel size 3
spec: Change whiten_kernel_size from 2 to 3 in CifarNet, which makes the fixed patch-statistics whitening convolution produce a larger number of channels (2*3*9 = 54). The whiten_width used by ConvGroup1 follows automatically. init_whiten already uses the kernel shape, so only the constant changes, but check the shape of the output map after padding.

title: Stratified class-balanced batches
spec: Replace the uniform randperm shuffle in CifarLoader.__iter__ with a class-stratified order: for each epoch, shuffle the indices of each of the 10 classes separately, then interleave them so every consecutive block of BATCH_SIZE contains roughly 153 samples from each class (round-robin across classes, then shuffle within the batch). Since CIFAR-10 is balanced this changes little in expectation but removes batch-to-batch label-count variance, which may reduce gradient noise in the BatchNorm statistics. Build the class index lists inside train() from the labels argument each run, not from any cached state.

title: AdamW for the whitening bias, norm biases and head in place of Nesterov SGD
spec: Replace optimizer1 (torch.optim.SGD with Nesterov momentum over the whiten bias, norm biases and head) with torch.optim.AdamW using the same parameter groups, base learning rates BIAS_LR for the bias groups and HEAD_LR for the head, betas (0.9, 0.99), and weight decay set so that the decoupled decay equals the current effective decay (wd / lr). Keep the linear decay of each group's lr to zero using the existing lr_factor logic, which multiplies initial_lr. Because Adam's update magnitude is not proportional to the gradient, the learning rates may need to be divided by roughly 10 to 20; try BIAS_LR scaled by 0.05 and HEAD_LR scaled by 0.05 as the first setting. Muon stays unchanged.

title: Residual connection inside each ConvGroup
spec: In ConvGroup.forward, after conv2 and norm2 and before the final SiLU, add the input of conv2 back to its output (x = x + residual) for the blocks where channels match. For block1 use a 1x1 projection or skip the residual. This adds identity paths around the second convolution and needs no new hyperparameters.

title: Trapezoidal learning-rate schedule for Muon
spec: Replace the linear decay of the Muon learning rate (lr_factor2 = 1 - step/total_train_steps for optimizer2) with a trapezoid: hold the factor at 1.0 for the first 40 percent of total_train_steps, then decay linearly to 0 at the final step. Implement it as lr_factor2 = min(1.0, (1 - step/total_train_steps) / 0.6). Apply the same trapezoid to the SGD head and bias groups, or keep those linear, as a separate choice. Leave the Muon target magnitude schedule inside the Newton-Schulz function unchanged so no compiled code is affected. This tests whether a longer high-LR plateau followed by a fast anneal helps a short run.

title: Train-mode BatchNorm recalibration on clean images after training
spec: At the end of train(), before returning, set the model to train mode with no gradient, reset every BatchNorm running_mean and running_var (or set BN momentum to None for cumulative averaging), and run a forward pass over a fixed set of about 10000 un-augmented training images (normalised, no flip, no translation, no colour jitter) in batches of 2000, so the BN running statistics match the clean test distribution rather than the jittered training distribution. Then call model.eval(). Only data already given to train() is used, so this respects the run-from-scratch rule. Cost is a few forward passes, well under 0.1 s.

title: Remove colour jitter
spec: Set the color_jitter config in train() to enabled False, so batch_color_jitter is skipped entirely. The brightness and contrast jitter costs a compiled kernel per epoch and may hurt a 7.65-epoch run that is underfitting rather than overfitting. This is a one-line config change and removes a source of noise from the input distribution.

title: Residual connection inside ConvGroup
spec: In ConvGroup.forward, add a skip connection around conv2: after norm2 and before the final activation, compute x = x + skip, where skip is the input to conv2 (the post-activation tensor from norm1 and SiLU). This needs the channel counts to match, which holds because conv2 maps channels_out to channels_out. Apply the activation after the addition. Only the forward method changes, and the BN parameters stay as they are.

title: Richer test-time augmentation
spec: In infer's _get_tta_logits, extend the views from the 3 shifted-and-base crops to a 5-view set: the original, reflect-padded crops at offsets (0,0), (0,2), (2,0), (2,2) and the centre. Concatenate them with their flips as before, and average the 10 logits. Keep the uncertain-quantile selection at 0.25, or try raising it to 0.5 if time allows. This is confined to predict() and does not affect training time.

title: Flat-then-decay learning-rate schedule
spec: Keep the learning rate constant at its base value for the first 40 percent of total_train_steps, then decay linearly to zero over the remaining 60 percent. Implement by replacing lr_factor2 = 1 - step * lr_factor2_base with lr_factor2 = min(1.0, 2.5 * (1 - step / total_train_steps)). Apply the same rule to lr_factor1 with whiten_bias_train_steps. This gives more time at high learning rate before annealing.

title: Label smoothing annealed to zero
spec: Make the label-smoothing value depend on step: pass a Python float smoothing = LABEL_SMOOTHING * (1 - step / total_train_steps) into forward_step, and use it in F.cross_entropy. Since the value changes each step, avoid recompilation by passing it as a 0-dim CUDA tensor (torch.tensor(value, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32)) and multiplying the cross-entropy target manually, or simply keep the constant and skip this idea if recompiles occur. The goal is to reduce label smoothing late in training, when the model should give sharp predictions.

title: Muon momentum warmup
spec: Replace the constant MUON_MOMENTUM in Muon.step with a ramp: momentum starts at 0.85 at step 0 and rises linearly to MUON_MOMENTUM (0.655 is the end value, so instead ramp from 0.5 up to 0.655 over the first 20 percent of total_train_steps, then hold). Implement by setting group['momentum'] from step_count / total_train_steps before the momentum multiply inside Muon.step. Nothing else changes.

title: Row-normalised Muon updates (NorMuon-style)
spec: After the Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation of each filter, track an exponential moving average of the squared row norms of each update, with decay 0.95, separately for each filter. Divide each update row by the square root of its running average, then rescale the whole update so its Frobenius norm matches the unnormalised orthogonalised update. This equalises the step size across output channels. The learning rate and momentum stay the same.

title: Progressive resolution with 28-pixel crops early
spec: For the first 50 percent of optimizer steps, feed random 28x28 crops taken from the augmented 32x32 batch, using the existing batch_crop logic with crop size 28. Switch to full 32x32 images for the remaining steps. The spatial chain 28 to 27 to 13 to 6 to 3 to 1 still ends at 1x1, so the head shape is unchanged. Compile each shape once, with dynamic=False. The learning-rate schedule and the 32-pixel test-time path stay as they are.

title: Muon on the classifier head
spec: Move the head weight out of the SGD group and into a second Muon optimizer. Treat it as a 10 by 256 matrix, with the same Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation, momentum and weight decay as the conv filters. Give it its own learning rate, HEAD_LR scaled by 0.1 as a starting point, with the same linear decay to zero. Keep the output scaling by 1 over the feature width unchanged. The biases stay on Nesterov SGD.

title: Short linear warmup then linear decay
spec: Multiply every learning rate by a warmup factor min(1, (step + 1) / warmup_steps) with warmup_steps = ceil(0.05 * total_train_steps), on top of the existing linear decay. Apply it in the training loop where lr_factor1 and lr_factor2 are computed, so the Muon and head groups ramp up over the first 5 percent of steps. This addresses the very large initial head and Muon steps early in training.

title: Larger random translation with reflect padding
spec: Increase TRANSLATE from 2 to 3 so the padded images are 38x38 and batch_crop draws offsets in [0, 6]. Make sure predict()'s TTA still uses views consistent with the new padding: in infer's _get_tta_logits, derive the crops from the same pad size, or keep TTA pad at 1 as it is. This increases augmentation diversity across 7.65 epochs. Check whether the accuracy gain outweighs the slightly larger input cost.

title: Half-precision test-time pass in one fused batch
spec: In predict, replace the separate initial pass and the uncertain-image pass with one forward over the stacked views of all test images, computed in a single compiled call with batch size 2000. Keep the 25 percent selection by confidence, but compute it from the first view's logits inside the same graph, and select the rows after the fact with torch.where instead of index assignment. The model is still not changed, and the output shape stays (N, 10). This removes the Python splitting and the extra copies.

title: Batch size 1024 with scaled learning rates
spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 1024 and multiply BIAS_LR, HEAD_LR and MUON_LR by sqrt(1024 / 1536) = 0.816. The loss uses reduction sum, and the optimizer already scales with batch-size-weighted decay (wd = WEIGHT_DECAY * batch size), so the weight decay term is recomputed automatically. This gives more optimizer steps per epoch and may improve the per-epoch sample efficiency, at the cost of more kernel launches.

title: Remove final MaxPool and flatten the 3x3 map into the head
spec: In CifarNet.layers, delete the final nn.MaxPool2d(3) so the last ConvGroup output is 256 x 3 x 3. Change the head to nn.Linear(256*3*3, 10, bias=False). In forward, x.view(len(x), -1) already flattens, and the division by x.size(-1) becomes division by the new flattened size, so keep that scaling. The head then sees spatial information it currently discards; the cost increase is confined to the 2304-by-10 linear layer and a slightly larger final norm and activation.

title: Post-training batch-norm recalibration on clean images
spec: At the end of train(), after the last optimizer step, switch to eval-free statistics collection: set every BatchNorm layer's momentum to None (cumulative average), reset its running_mean and running_var, then run one no-grad pass over the unaugmented normalised training images in batches of 2000 with model.train() so the running statistics match un-jittered, un-flipped, un-cropped data. Then return. Training-time running stats are averaged over augmented, cropped batches, so this corrects a mismatch that matters for the test-time views. The pass is cheap and is inside the timed train() call.

title: Loss-weighted hard-example sampling
spec: Keep the step count fixed at EPOCHS * len(train_loader). Keep a per-sample loss vector of length 50000 on the GPU, initialised to 1.0. Change forward_step to return per-sample losses (reduction none), sum them for backward, and write the detached losses back into the vector at the batch indices after each step. At the start of each epoch, draw 50000 indices with torch.multinomial, with replacement, using weights equal to the stored loss raised to the power 0.5. Chunk them into batches of BATCH_SIZE as before. Flip, translate and jitter stay unchanged.

title: Stride-2 convolution replaces the block max-pool
spec: In ConvGroup, replace the MaxPool2d(2) after conv1 with a learned stride-2 3x3 convolution from channels_in to channels_out, with padding 1 and no bias. Keep the rest of the group as is, so the norm, activation and conv2 order is unchanged. The layer that follows the group then takes stride-2 features. Make the first group's stride-2 conv operate on the whitened input as before. Initialise the new stride-2 convolution with the same Dirac scheme used for the existing convolutions, applied to the first channels.

title: Shape-aware Muon learning rate
spec: Scale each filter's Muon update by a per-layer factor max(1, out_channels / in_channels) ** 0.5 (computed once in Muon.__init__ from reshaped_dims, stored in filter_params_meta). Multiply the orthogonalised update for that parameter by this factor before the foreach subtraction. This equalises effective step sizes between the wide 256-channel layers and the narrow 64-channel layer. Keep MUON_LR unchanged.

title: Orthogonalise each 3x3 conv per spatial tap
spec: Change how Muon sees 4-D convolution filters. Instead of reshaping a weight of shape (out, in, 3, 3) to (out, in*9) and orthogonalising that matrix, reshape it to (out*3, in*3), i.e. treat each row-tap pair as a matrix of size out-by-in per kernel row, or equivalently orthogonalise the (out, in) matrix of each of the 9 spatial taps separately by permuting to (9, out, in) and batching. Implement this inside the Muon meta data: store the permutation and pad to the larger shape used by _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, then un-permute after the Newton-Schulz step. Keep the norm-scaling rule, the LR, the momentum and the weight decay as they are.

title: Low-resolution warm-up
spec: For the first 20 percent of training steps, downsample each batch from 32 by 32 to 24 by 24 with bilinear interpolation (antialias on), then use the full 32 by 32 inputs for the remaining steps. Make the training loop select the resize path by step, and keep the same batch size and labels. Because the whitening conv and pooling layers accept any size, the network needs no architectural change, but compile separate graphs for the two input sizes.

title: Five-shift TTA views
spec: Extend the TTA views in _get_tta_logits from three translations (center, top-left, bottom-right) to five by adding top-right and bottom-left 2-pixel reflect crops, all with their flips. Average the logits over all ten views for the uncertain images. Predicted cost increases only for the uncertain quarter of the test set.

title: Remove colour jitter
spec: Set the color_jitter entry in the training augmentation dictionary to enabled False and remove the brightness and contrast perturbation. The flip and translation augmentations stay as they are. This is an ablation that checks whether the colour jitter helps at this training length or only costs time.

title: Momentum warmup for Muon
spec: Start MUON_MOMENTUM at 0.5 and ramp it linearly to its final value of 0.655 over the first 20 percent of training steps, then hold it constant. Update group['momentum'] for the Muon param group inside the train loop before each optimizer step. Keep the Nesterov form and all other Muon settings unchanged.

title: Label smoothing ramp
spec: Start label smoothing at 0.0 and increase it linearly to LABEL_SMOOTHING (0.09) over the first 30 percent of training steps, then hold it. Pass the current value into the loss function through a tensor argument, or recompute the smoothed targets manually so the compiled forward step does not recompile on every change. Keep the loss reduction as sum.

title: Learned BatchNorm scale
spec: In the BatchNorm class, remove the line that sets self.weight.requires_grad to False so the scale parameter is learned. Keep the initial value of one. Update the optimizer parameter groups so the norm scales join the bias group (the code already selects parameters with 'norm' in the name, so they will be picked up automatically). The rest of training is unchanged.

title: Residual projection skip in each ConvGroup
spec: In ConvGroup, add a skip path that takes the block input, applies max-pool with kernel 2, and a 1x1 convolution (bias-free, channels_out outputs), and adds it to the output of norm2 before the final SiLU. Initialise the 1x1 projection weights to zero so the block starts identical to the current one. The rest of the network is unchanged.

title: Three-stage progressive resizing
spec: Extend the existing low-resolution warm-up into three stages instead of one. For the first 20 percent of total steps, interpolate inputs to 20x20 with antialiased bilinear. From 20 to 55 percent of steps, use 24x24. For the remaining steps use the full 32x32. Compute the stage boundaries from total_train_steps and keep the interpolation inside the training loop, as now. Because torch.compile is set with dynamic=False, each new input size will trigger one recompile, so warm up the forward_step at each size in the untimed first call if needed, or accept one extra recompile per size that is excluded from the timed runs only if it happens during the untimed call. Measure whether the extra stage helps.

title: Learnable blend of max and average pooling
spec: Replace each nn.MaxPool2d(2) in ConvGroup with a custom module that computes a learnable scalar alpha, initialised to 1.0, and returns alpha times max pooling plus (1 minus alpha) times average pooling, both with kernel 2 and stride 2. The scalar is a parameter with requires_grad True and no weight decay. Keep the module in half precision with the rest of the network so the model.half() loop still applies. Also replace the final nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with the same blend at global size. This lets the network choose between the two pooling types per stage, and it adds only a few parameters and almost no compute.

title: Orthogonalised Muon update for the head
spec: Move model.head.weight out of the Nesterov SGD group and into the Muon optimizer, treating its 10x256 matrix as a 2D filter. Keep its learning rate at HEAD_LR scaled to the Muon scale, for example MUON_LR times 0.5, and keep the same linear decay to zero. Remove head_lr from the SGD param_configs. The head then receives Newton-Schulz orthogonalised updates, which may suit a short-horizon linear classifier better than raw SGD. The existing filter_params list only takes 4D tensors, so add the head to a separate Muon instance or extend the filter test to include 2D parameters named head.

title: Translation of 3 pixels
spec: Change TRANSLATE from 2 to 3, so the reflect-padded images are 38 by 38 and random crops of 32 by 32 move by up to three pixels in each direction. The batch_crop function already computes its offsets from the padding size, so no other code changes are required. Keep the TTA padding at its current value.

title: Layer-wise Muon learning-rate multipliers
spec: Keep a single Muon optimizer but split the filter parameters into three param groups by block: conv weights of ConvGroup 1 use a multiplier of 0.6, ConvGroup 2 uses 1.0, and ConvGroup 3 uses 1.4 on top of MUON_LR. Each group keeps the same linear decay and the same weight decay. The Muon step currently reads group["lr"] from param_groups[0] only, so change the step to loop over groups, or run one Muon instance per block. The idea is that the early high-resolution filters and the late wide filters may want different step sizes under orthogonalised updates.

title: EMA of weights for the final model
spec: Keep an exponential moving average of all trainable parameters, updated after each optimizer step with decay 0.995 once the first 50 percent of steps are done (copy the raw weights before that point).
